findings.location: Feed picture click in Program mode
findings.issue: One click on a feed picture is specified as both 'cut Program to this feed' and 'focus this tile'. The focused tile is the target of ⌃⌥F/⌃⌥C and the tools, so adjusting monitoring on the NEXT feed cuts it on air.
findings.evidence: main-expanded legend 2: 'Click a picture or press ⌃1/⌃2 to cut'. monitor-tools keyboard card: 'Click a tile to focus it (blue ring). Shortcuts act on the focused tile only, as today.' MonitorWorkspaceShell.swift: TapGesture().onEnded { focusedTile = index }.
findings.scenario: T4: mid-meeting the user clicks Feed 2 to turn on zebra before cutting, and Zoom immediately cuts to Feed 2 with an unchecked frame.
findings.recommendation: Picture click only focuses or selects. Cuts come only from explicit cut controls: toolbar cut buttons, cut bar, ⌃1–⌃4, dropdown thumbnails, and a dedicated 'Cut' pill on non-air pictures.
alternatives: Double-click a picture to cut
⌥-click to cut, with a hint in the hover toolbar
Click arms the cut (green 'NEXT') and a second click or Return takes it, like a switcher's preview/program

findings.issue: The live window has no visible Start or Stop control for a feed. The expanded strip header has only a status badge and ⋯; the r3 toolbar dropped Start/Stop; the ⋯ popover footer has Rename/Diagnostics/Remove only. Starting and stopping live only in Feed ▸ ⌘↩ and the dropdown. Only the 'Feed stopped' state (states page) shows a Start Feed button.
findings.evidence: r3.js strip(expanded) header: name, cam, 'Live · fmt' badge, ⋯ button. r3.js toolbar(): title, cuts, layout, collapse, record; no Start/Stop. main-collapsed ⋯ footer: Rename…, Diagnostics…, Remove Camera.
findings.scenario: T5/T2: after a recording session the user wants to stop Feed 2's capture to free the device or GPU and can't find how without the menu.
findings.recommendation: Put a Start/Stop Feed control in each strip header (expanded) and in the collapsed row's hover controls. In automatic mode show 'Automatic' plus Retry instead.
alternatives: Make the 'Live · 2160p59.94' badge a pop-up button with Stop Feed / Restart
A toolbar Start/Stop that acts on the selected feed, labelled with its name

findings.issue: Stopping a feed silently ends that feed's recording, but no design says so or asks first. ⌘↩ is a single keystroke and the Feed menu or dropdown 'Stop Feed' sits above the recording rows.
findings.evidence: AppModel.stop(): manuallyStoppedFeeds.insert…; feedCoordinator.stop(selectedFeedID); recordingModel.stop(feedID: selectedFeedID). menubar (b)/(g) 'Stop Feed ⌘↩' with 'Stop Recording 12:31' listed separately below.
findings.scenario: T2: the user wants to briefly stop the camera feed (e.g. to change input) during a backup take and ends the backup recording without realising.
findings.recommendation: When the feed is recording, label it 'Stop Feed and Recording…' and ask once ('Feed 1 is recording 38:12. Stopping the feed ends the take.' [Keep Recording] [Stop Both]). Same in the strip control from L1-02.
alternatives: Disable Stop Feed while recording with 'Stop the recording first'
Make ⌘↩ require the window to be frontmost and never act from the dropdown

findings.issue: In Program mode the dropdown offers 'Stop Feeds', plural, implying every source stops. The code's stop() stops only the selected feed (and its recording); the other headless Program sources and their recordings keep running.
findings.evidence: menubar.html Program dropdown row 'Stop Feeds' ⌘↩. AppModel.stop() only calls feedCoordinator.stop(selectedFeedID) and recordingModel.stop(feedID: selectedFeedID); startFeed() in Program mode starts every enabled source.
findings.scenario: T4 after a two-camera meeting: the user presses Stop Feeds, sees Feed 1 stop, and leaves. Feed 2 keeps capturing and recording to the drive.
findings.recommendation: Decide the model. Either 'Stop All Feeds' truly stops all sources (a model change, matching how Program starts all), or label it 'Stop Feed 1' and show the other sources still running. Program-mode start/stop should be symmetric.
alternatives: Separate rows: 'Stop Feed 1' and 'Stop All Feeds'
End Meeting command: stop all feeds and recordings with one confirmation

findings.location: Effect toggles while Zoom is live (strip chips, ⋯ popover, dropdown Effects submenu)
findings.issue: Changing Downscale, Color or Frame rate changes the published format. The producer drains and renegotiates the camera transport, which can blank or hiccup Zoom. No design warns about this, and the existing 'Applying change…' feedback state is gone. A LUT toggle doesn't change the format and is safe, but nothing tells the two apart.
findings.evidence: README: 'The producer stops and drains its camera transport before negotiating a changed output format, then resumes delivery.' Current AppliedPipelineState shows 'Applying change…'. 'Applying' appears on no r3 page. The Effects submenu (single/menubar) lists all four toggles identically.
findings.scenario: T3: during a meeting the user unticks '3 · Color 4:2:0' to test 10-bit and Zoom freezes or blacks for a moment in front of the call.
findings.recommendation: Mark format-changing effects (2, 3, 4) with 'Changes Zoom's format · brief interruption' when a consumer is active, ask before applying while ON AIR, and restore an 'Applying change…' transitional state on the strip chips and result line. Keep the LUT toggle instant.
alternatives: Defer format changes while ON AIR: 'Apply when Zoom stops using the camera'
Lock format-changing effects while the camera is in use and show why

findings.location: Per-feed effect chips in Program mode
findings.issue: Strips present each feed's output effects as independent, but Program's transport contract is recomputed from whichever feed is on air at each applied cut. Feeds with different format settings (or LUT on vs off) can make every cut reconfigure the Program camera. Nothing shows the Program output format or flags a mismatch.
findings.evidence: AppModel feedCoordinator.onProgramCutApplied → reconcileProgramTransportDemand(); programContract(configuration: producer's configuration…). main-expanded: Feed 1 fx [LUT,1080p,4:2:0], Feed 2 [1080p,4:2:0], with no Program format shown.
findings.scenario: T4: Feed 2 is set to 4:2:2 10-bit (Color off). Every Auto cut to Feed 2 renegotiates Zoom's camera format, producing repeated glitches the user can't trace.
findings.recommendation: Show 'Program output: 1080p 29.97 · 4:2:0' in the sidebar Output section, and flag strips whose output format differs ('Differs from Program: cuts may interrupt'). Consider a single Program format that sources conform to.
alternatives: Force matching format effects across Program sources (lock 2–4 to Program)
Warn once when entering Program mode with mismatched feeds

findings.location: After the meeting: Zoom closes while a backup take is running
findings.issue: Today, recording counts as demand, so when Zoom closes the feed and the backup take keep running indefinitely. No page designs this 'meeting ended, still recording' state. Only the proposed NEW auto-stop toggle covers it.
findings.evidence: AppModel.reconcileAutomaticFeed(): demand(camera || programRequested || recording); case .stop: guard …, !recording. No page contains 'meeting ended', 'Zoom closed' or an equivalent. menubar/settings show 'Stop when the last camera app closes' as NEW only.
findings.scenario: T2: the user ends the Zoom call and closes the laptop lid or walks away. The take keeps filling the 8TB drive for hours and the next meeting's backup lands in the same huge file.
findings.recommendation: Design a post-meeting state: an orange banner in the dropdown and window plus a notification, 'Zoom stopped using Ultracam · Feed 1 still recording 1:02:31' [Stop Recording] [Keep Recording]. Make 'Stop when the last camera app closes' default-on when 'Record with camera apps' is on.
alternatives: Auto-stop after N minutes without a consumer (setting)
Menu bar icon pulses or turns orange when recording with no consumer
findings.verified: AppModel.swift:1001 demand includes recording; :1032 never stops while recording

findings.location: Strip after Stop / sidebar Recent Takes
findings.issue: There's no post-take state. After Stop, the strip goes back to 'Ready', with no 'Saved · file name · duration · Show in Finder'. Recent Takes rows have no reveal action (round 2 had one), so 'find the files' needs the dropdown or Record menu 'Show Recordings in Finder', which opens a folder, not the take. The current app keeps final take statistics visible until the next take.
findings.evidence: r3.js sidebar() take row: icon + name only, no button. states expanded 'Ready' strip has no last-take line. README: 'Final take statistics remain visible until the next take.'
findings.scenario: T5: after recording a 40-minute interview on two cameras, the user wants to check both files and drag them into an editor. They must open the folder and hunt by timestamp.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Saved' strip state ('Saved · Feed 1_2026-10-20_09-41-03_001.mov · 38:12 · 56 GB · 0 dropped' [Show in Finder] [Quick Look]) that persists until the next take. Give Recent Takes rows reveal-on-hover and drag-out.
alternatives: A one-line 'Last take' in the collapsed strip
Notification on finalize with a Show action

findings.location: Rename… / Add Camera while anything is running
findings.issue: Rename (⋯ footer, Feed menu 'Rename Feed 1…') and the sidebar '+' are drawn enabled during a live, recording session. The model only allows rename, add, remove and output-mode changes when every source is stopped and nothing is recording, so T8 'rename one camera without touching the other' fails silently.
findings.evidence: AppModel.renameFeed/addFeed guard canEditFeedTopology; FeedLifecycleDemandPolicy.canEditTopology = !loading && !sourceActive && !recordingActive. main-collapsed ⋯ footer 'Rename…' enabled; app-menus row('Rename Feed 1…') enabled; r3.js sidebar plus icon not disabled. Only app-menus 'Add Camera · stop to change' is disabled.
findings.scenario: T8: during a take the user tries to rename 'Feed 2' to 'B-cam'. Nothing happens, or the field reverts.
findings.recommendation: Disable with the reason everywhere ('Stop all feeds and recordings to rename'), or better, relax the model so renaming is metadata-only (it affects the next take's folder and file names and the virtual camera name).
alternatives: Allow rename while running but defer applying it until feeds stop, with a 'pending' badge

findings.location: Going from one camera to two-camera switching (Output mode) / first Zoom setup
findings.issue: Moving to Program is a hidden, multi-step flow: stop everything, + Add Camera, choose its input in ⋯, switch Output mode in Settings or the Program menu (locked while running), then choose a DIFFERENT camera in Zoom ('Ultracam · Program' instead of 'Ultracam · Feed 1'). No page guides it or tells the user to re-pick the camera in Zoom. The onboarding card also never says which camera name to choose in Zoom.
findings.evidence: VirtualCameraRegistryPublishing: Separate mode publishes 'Ultracam · <feed>', Program publishes 'Ultracam · Program'. settings Camera pane lists names without a call to action. app-menus Program ▸ Output Mode is disabled ('change while stopped'). states first-launch steps: install → input → LUT → folder, with no Zoom step.
findings.scenario: T4: the user switches to Program for a two-camera call. Zoom keeps showing 'Ultracam · Feed 1' (now no longer published), the call shows black, and the user doesn't know why.
findings.recommendation: Add a guided 'Set Up Switching…' sheet (add camera → input → mode) and, after any mode change or first install, a persistent banner: 'In Zoom › Video, choose Ultracam · Program'. Add that as the last onboarding step.
alternatives: Keep a stable 'Ultracam' camera name in both modes (a model change) so Zoom never needs re-selecting
A status bar Output popover hint when the expected camera has no consumer for 30 s

findings.location: First run: Install Camera → System Settings approval
findings.issue: No state covers the gap between 'Install Camera' and the user approving the extension in System Settings (the installer has a pending state), or an approval that's declined or ignored. The onboarding step goes from an Install button straight to done.
findings.evidence: ExtensionInstaller has `pending` and a status text; the current UI disables Install/Remove while pending. states first-launch step 1 'Install the Ultracam camera … Approve …' shows only an Install button; settings Camera shows only installed or not.
findings.scenario: T1: the user clicks Install, the macOS approval prompt is dismissed or hidden behind windows, and Ultracam gives no hint what to do next. Zoom has no camera.
findings.recommendation: Design 'Waiting for approval' (spinner, 'Approve Ultracam Camera in System Settings › General › Login Items & Extensions › Camera Extensions' [Open System Settings]), 'Approval needed again', and 'Installed: reopen Zoom's camera menu' states, both in onboarding and in sidebar Output.
alternatives: A short animated how-to in the onboarding card

findings.location: Overriding Auto during a Program meeting
findings.issue: A manual cut with Auto on is passed to the director as a manual override, so Auto keeps running and may cut away again after the minimum shot. No page explains this or offers a 'Hold' that pauses Auto without turning it off, although NaturalTalkingHeadSettings.manualHold exists and the director honours it. The only way to keep a shot is to turn Auto off and remember to turn it back on.
findings.evidence: AppModel.requestProgramCut → autoSwitcherBridge.manualOverride(…). director.rs: `if self.config.manual_hold { return None; }`. AppSettingsStore.manualHold (not shown in r3 settings, which the agent judged runtime state). No page contains 'Hold'.
findings.scenario: T4: the guest starts a long answer and the user cuts to Feed 2 to stay on them. Twenty seconds later Auto cuts back to the host mid-sentence.
findings.recommendation: Add 'Hold' (toggle, e.g. ⌃⌥H) next to Auto in the toolbar cut group, cut bar and dropdown, mapped to manualHold. After a manual cut, show the shot timer state 'Manual cut · Auto may cut after 10 s'.
alternatives: Manual cut auto-holds for N seconds (setting)
Long-press a cut button to cut and hold

findings.location: Effect chips in the channel strip
findings.issue: The LUT / 1080p / 4:2:0 / 29.97 chips read as status badges. Nothing shows they're toggles (no hover or pressed affordance, no tooltip), so T3 'turn the LUT off' from the window isn't discoverable. The documented paths are the ⋯ popover or the dropdown submenu.
findings.evidence: r3.js fxChips(): plain spans styled as badges. spec §4 says 'effect chips = Toggle(.button)', but nothing on the pages communicates it.
findings.scenario: T3: mid-meeting the user looks at the strip to turn the LUT off, doesn't recognise the chip as a button, and opens Settings instead.
findings.recommendation: Render chips as a segmented row of toggle buttons with hover, pressed and tooltip states ('LUT on: click to bypass the LUT'), or replace them with a compact 'Effects ▾' pop-up button listing the four ordered toggles.
alternatives: Keep the chips as status only and add an 'Effects' button beside them

findings.issue: The toolbar's primary recording control shows only '■ 12:31 · 2', with no verb. While recording it's Stop All, at rest presumably Record All, but the label never says which, and it sits beside the per-strip 'Stop' (recording) and 'Pause'.
findings.evidence:
r3.js toolbar(): `
${ic('stop')}${recLabel}
`, with recLabel '12:31 · 2'. standalone wrote 'Stop All · 12:31' locally.
findings.scenario: T5: at the end of a session the user isn't sure whether the red pill stops both cameras or only the focused one, and stops the cameras one by one in the strips.
findings.recommendation: Always include the verb and scope: 'Record All' at rest, 'Stop All · 12:31 · 2' while recording (as standalone.html does). The tooltip lists which feeds are affected.
alternatives: A split button: main = Stop All, menu = per-feed stop/pause

findings.location: Automatic mode: opening the window before a meeting
findings.issue: A visible preview counts as demand in automatic mode, so opening the main window to check framing starts capture and GPU work. The 'Automatic mode waiting / Waiting for a camera app' picture card can't occur in a visible main window with preview on. The menubar agent handled this for the dropdown only ('Show Live Preview').
findings.evidence: README: 'Start for a camera app or a visible preview.' AppModel.reconcileAutomaticFeed(): policy.previewDemand(legacyVisible || monitorDemand…). states §3 'Automatic mode waiting' card shows a main-window picture placeholder.
findings.scenario: T2: the user opens Ultracam an hour before the meeting to check settings. The feed starts and stays running (GPU and fans) until they hide the preview or close the window.
findings.recommendation: Either show the waiting placeholder with an explicit 'Show Live Preview (starts the feed)' button in the window too, matching the dropdown, or keep the demand rule and say so on the picture: 'Preview started the feed · it stops when you close the window'.
alternatives: Let the main window open in a 'waiting' layout until the user asks for preview

findings.location: Record All when some feeds aren't running
findings.issue: Recording needs a running feed ('Start this feed before recording it'). Record All with one feed stopped or without signal records only part of the session, and no page shows what Record All will actually include before or after pressing it.
findings.evidence: RecordingModel: 'Start this feed before recording it. Only an active source feed can produce media.' four-up: Feed 3 'No HDMI signal' with Record disabled; the toolbar shows '12:31 · 3' with no indication that Feed 3 is excluded.
findings.scenario: T5: the user presses Record All for a three-camera interview without noticing Feed 3 has no signal, and loses the third angle.
findings.recommendation: Label it with scope ('Record All · 2 of 3 ready') and, when pressed with an unready feed, flag it: an orange 'Feed 3 not recording · no signal' in the status bar and the strip, plus an optional confirmation.
alternatives: Record All arms unready feeds and starts them automatically when their signal arrives

findings.issue: Coverage matrix of round-3 states
findings.evidence: rendered text of all 13 pages; code refs per finding

legend.designed: drawn on a round-3 page (page noted)
legend.implied: follows from a stated rule or another drawn state, not drawn
legend.n/a: component has no role in this condition

stopped / idle.toolbar: missing: r3 toolbar has no Start/Stop and no idle Record All

paused.toolbar: implied: standalone shows Stop All + Pause All, mixed label undefined
paused.menubar_icon: missing: paused vs recording dot undefined

recording failed.status_bar: missing: error example is failed start

automatic · preview-only demand.dropdown: implied: Show Live Preview leads here

disk low.strip_expanded: missing: time-left text not shown orange

cut pending.strip_expanded: missing: Cut to button has no pending state

matrix.notes: Quit sheet is drawn (states 6.6). Frozen/clean/zoom picture states are drawn in monitor-tools. App menus are drawn in one state only; enabling rules elsewhere are implied by spec §5.

findings.recommendation: Fill the P0/P1 missing cells in round 4; rows with no designed cell are listed as findings below.

findings.location: strip + picture + status bar: HDMI lost during a take
findings.issue: No design for 'recording but no signal'. The recorder rejects no-signal frames while the take stays open, but the UI shows either REC or No signal, never both.
findings.evidence: SourceRecordingAdapter.swift:59-63 (signalValid=false → reject()); states 1.3 Recording and 1.9 Waiting for HDMI are separate cards; no combined state on any page
findings.scenario: Cable bumped mid-meeting: the strip still says Recording 00:31:44 while nothing is written for 40 s; the user trusts a backup with a hole in it.
findings.recommendation: Add a combined state: strip 'REC · no signal 0:42 · not writing frames' (red text, counter keeps running), picture No-signal overlay keeps the REC pill, status bar error segment, attention dot. Define whether the take continues or splits when signal returns.
alternatives: Auto-pause the take on signal loss and resume on return (needs runtime change)
Split into a new take when signal returns
findings.verified: SourceRecordingAdapter appendRawVideo: guard signalValid else reject()

findings.issue: The disk sequence stops at '2 min left: recording will stop when the drive is full'. The state at full (writer failure on every take on that drive, what was saved, whether Recover applies) is not designed.
findings.evidence: states 4.5 and menubar g end at the warning; RecordingModel.swift:361-378 a failed flush throws writerFailure(lastError ?? 'Recording stopped after a source error.'); no disk-capacity check exists in code
findings.scenario: Two feeds back up to 8TB; it fills at 1:42:10. Both strips show the generic source-error text, or nothing distinguishable, and the user doesn't know the takes were saved up to the last fragment.
findings.recommendation: Design 'Stopped · drive full · saved to 1:41:58 (last fragment)' per strip, a single status-bar error naming the drive, the attention dot, and a recovery note if finalization failed. Map the writer error text to a plain 'drive full' message.
alternatives: Stop takes cleanly at ~1 min left, before the drive is actually full (needs runtime support; time-left is NEW)

findings.location: effect chips / Processing switch while a consumer is live
findings.issue: There is no transitional state for an effect or Processing change. The current app shows 'Applying change…' while pipelineEnabledApplied differs from the selection, and the producer drains and renegotiates format on effect changes. Round 3 dropped both the label and any warning.
findings.evidence: FeedInterface.swift:431-444 AppliedPipelineState ('Applying change…'); README: 'The producer stops and drains its camera transport before negotiating a changed output format'; grep 'Applying' finds nothing in r3
findings.scenario: Mid-call the user toggles Downscale on Feed 1; Zoom's picture blanks or reconnects and the UI gives no sign that this was expected or when it's done.
findings.recommendation: Add 'Applying…' to the strip chips and result line, and an 'Output restarting' badge on the picture. Warn before format-changing toggles while a consumer is connected ('Zoom may briefly lose video').
alternatives: Defer format-changing toggles until the camera is not in use
Mark which effects are live-safe (LUT) vs format-changing (Downscale, Color, Frame rate)

findings.issue: There's no 'saved' state. After Finishing, the Ready card resets the counter to 00:00:00. The current app keeps final take statistics visible until the next take, and that's the user's confirmation the backup exists.
findings.evidence: README 'Final take statistics remain visible until the next take'; states 1.1 Ready shows 00:00:00; states 1.6 Failed keeps stats but no success equivalent
findings.scenario: After a meeting the user stops recording and sees a zeroed strip: did it save? They must open Finder to check.
findings.recommendation: Strip state 'Saved · 38:12 · 56.1 GB · Show in Finder' (collapsed: 'Saved 38:12'), kept until the next take; Record still enabled.
alternatives: Transient banner plus Recent Takes highlight

findings.location: sidebar Output / onboarding step 1 during camera install
findings.issue: The extension approval-pending state is missing. The installer moves through 'Requesting activation…' to 'Approve Ultracam in System Settings → … Camera Extensions', but round 3 only draws not-installed and installed.
findings.evidence: ExtensionInstaller.swift:140-161 (pending, status strings); states 4.2/4.3 and the settings Camera pane have no pending or needs-approval visual
findings.scenario: First launch: the user clicks Install Camera and nothing visible changes while macOS waits for approval; Zoom doesn't list Ultracam.
findings.recommendation: Add Output states 'Requesting…' (spinner, buttons disabled) and 'Needs approval' (Open System Settings button). Echo them in the onboarding card, status bar and dropdown.

findings.issue: 'Device gone' is not distinguished from 'no HDMI signal'. Only the first-run no-device card exists. The app reports 'Connect the UltraStudio and refresh inputs.' and disables Start when the selected device is missing, and a pull mid-take ends in a source error.
findings.evidence: AppModel.swift:966 automatic status; canStartFeed requires a device; no device-removal handling in code (no matches); states 3.6 No HDMI signal assumes the device is present
findings.scenario: The USB-C/Thunderbolt cable to the UltraStudio is unplugged: the UI says 'No HDMI signal, check the FX3', pointing at the wrong cable.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Device disconnected' state (picture + strip + attention dot) with Refresh, separate from no signal. Define the mid-take outcome (take finalized to last fragment).

findings.location: green NEXT tally and dashed CUTTING
findings.issue: NEXT has three definitions. Main pages show NEXT permanently on the non-air feed with 'cut after 10 s'. States uses NEXT for the director's queued cut and dashed CUTTING for a manual pending cut. Spec §5 defines NEXT as any queued cut (pending feed). The model only knows pendingCut/pendingCutTime (any queued cut) and pendingDirectorCut, with no predicted next feed when nothing is queued.
findings.evidence: SwitcherCoordinator.swift:28-31,131-134; states 3.2/3.3; spec Picture tally table 'Next = Queued cut (pending feed)'; main-expanded Feed 2 NEXT with no pending cut
findings.scenario: In a two-camera manual meeting Feed 2 always wears green NEXT, so green stops meaning anything. When a cut really is queued there's no visible change.
findings.recommendation: One rule: no ring when nothing is queued; green NEXT only while pendingCut != nil (with the time from pendingCutTime). Drop the separate dashed state or keep it for manual cuts only, and drop predicted 'after 10 s' copy unless the director exposes it.
alternatives: Neutral 'Preview' outline for the idle non-air feed, broadcast-switcher style

findings.location: Program when the on-air source stops or every source is unhealthy
findings.issue: Two Program transitions are undesigned: stopping (or losing) the feed currently on air, and the evaluator's noHealthyFeed state, where Zoom ends up with black after 0.5 s.
findings.evidence: SwitcherCoordinator.swift:6-11 SwitcherEvaluation.noHealthyFeed; AppModel.swift:929 setProgramSourceHealth(false); states 3.12 says only 'a stopped feed has no tally'
findings.scenario: The on-air FX3 overheats and drops out. Does Program cut to Feed 2, hold the last frame or go black? The operator can't tell from the UI what Zoom now sees.
findings.recommendation: Define and draw: (a) on-air source lost → automatic cut to a healthy source or 'Program: no source · Zoom receiving black' (red, status bar error, attention dot); (b) a warning when Stop Feed targets the on-air feed.

findings.issue: Round 3 has nowhere to show automaticFeedStatus outside the dropdown. Its sub-states (preview-only demand, camera in use, restoring LUT, device missing, retry needed) have no window design. The old UI showed the status under the toggle.
findings.evidence: AppModel.swift:958-967 (six status strings); sidebar Automation rows are bare switches; states 1.11 covers only failed start
findings.scenario: With automatic mode on, the user opens the window and sees capture running with no camera app open; nothing says the visible preview is what's keeping it running.
findings.recommendation: Add a status line under 'Start with camera apps' in the sidebar, mirrored in the strip header badge (e.g. 'Automatic · kept alive by preview').

findings.location: toolbar Record All / Stop All control
findings.issue: The primary record control is drawn only while recording (Stop All · 12:31 · N). Idle, disabled (no live feed or no folder), finishing, mixed paused and all-paused states are missing.
findings.evidence: main-expanded/standalone/four-up toolbars all recording; menus show Record All disabled ('start a feed first') but the toolbar never does
findings.scenario: Before a meeting the user looks for Record and the toolbar shows a red button with no label they've seen before.
findings.recommendation: Draw all toolbar record states in states.html and spec §5, with labels: Record All / Stop All · 12:31 · 2 / Finishing… / Resume All when all are paused.

findings.issue: There's no starting state anywhere. The capture path reports 'Opening UltraStudio…' and passes through Connecting, Waiting for HDMI and Ready before Live.
findings.evidence: FeedInterface.swift:361-367 FeedStateLabel; AppModel.swift:685 'Opening UltraStudio…'
findings.scenario: Pressing ⌘↩ shows nothing for a second; the user presses it again and stops the feed.
findings.recommendation: Strip badge 'Starting…' with a spinner, picture placeholder 'Opening UltraStudio…', Start control disabled until established.

findings.issue: Preview error with Retry preview (existing PreviewErrorNotice) and the 'insufficient presentation capacity' state for extra monitor windows are both absent from round 3.
findings.evidence: FeedInterface.swift:119-136; README Monitor tools 'Additional windows can report insufficient presentation capacity'
findings.scenario: The preview renderer fails: the picture stays black with no explanation, though camera output is fine.
findings.recommendation: Picture overlay 'Preview failed · camera output continues · Retry Preview'; detached window 'Monitor unavailable · close another window'.

findings.issue: The loading state ('Restoring your LUT…') is missing. Start is disabled while it runs and the effects are disabled.
findings.evidence: AppModel canStartFeed (!loading); automaticFeedStatus 'Restoring your LUT…'; LUTControls 'Loading LUT…'
findings.scenario: Launch, immediately ⌘↩: nothing happens and there's no reason given.
findings.recommendation: Strip LUT chip spinner + 'Restoring LUT…'; Start disabled with tooltip.

findings.location: menu bar icon and status bar precedence
findings.issue: Icon states for paused, finishing and starting are undefined, as is precedence when recording and attention coincide. Stopped, automatic waiting, finishing, recording-failed and extension-pending status bar states aren't drawn either.
findings.evidence: states 6.4 icon strip (6 states); states §5 status bar (5 states, 'worst wins' only for warning/error)
findings.scenario: During a paused backup the icon still shows a red dot, so the user believes it's recording.
findings.recommendation: Add a precedence table (error > attention > recording > paused > live > waiting > stopped) and draw paused (orange dot) and finishing.

findings.issue: Neither the code nor the design handles system sleep during a live feed or recording.
findings.evidence: no willSleep/didWake handling in Sources; no state on any page
findings.scenario: A laptop lid closes mid-take: capture and the encoder stop abruptly and the take needs recovery; on wake nothing explains why.
findings.recommendation: Runtime: hold a power assertion while recording or published (NEW). UI: 'Keeping your Mac awake while recording' in the status popover, plus a post-wake banner when a take was interrupted.

findings.location: cut controls while a cut is pending or the target is skipped
findings.issue: Only the picture shows pending or skipped state. The toolbar cut buttons, strip 'Cut to Feed N', sidebar camera rows and dropdown cut thumbnails have no pending or disabled-with-reason state.
findings.evidence: states 3.3/3.5 picture-only; toolbar() and strip() builders have no pending branch
findings.scenario: The user presses the toolbar Feed 2 button, sees no change for a frame-boundary wait, and presses again.
findings.recommendation: Mirror pending (pulsing or dashed) and skipped (disabled with reason in the tooltip) on every cut control.

findings.issue: Several key transitions are not specified: Recording→Finishing→Saved→Ready (what the strip shows at each step); Failed→new take (does the record button reuse the folder, keep the failed stats?); Automatic start failed→Retry→fails again (one attempt per session, then what?); disk low→full→stopped; no signal mid-take→signal returns (same take or new take?); bypass on→off while live (format renegotiation).
findings.evidence: states captions describe single frames only; no transition notes in spec §5
findings.scenario: Engineers implement each state differently because the in-between behavior is undefined.
findings.recommendation: Add a transition table to spec §5: state → trigger → next state → what each component shows, with duration and cancellability.
alternatives: Small state diagrams per component

findings.issue: Effect changes renegotiate output format mid-meeting and no round-3 state warns or shows progress (see L10-03).
findings.evidence: README format renegotiation; no 'Applying' state in r3

findings.issue: Round-3 toolbars and expanded strips have no Start/Stop Feed control at all while live (only the stopped-strip state and the menus/dropdown have it), so per-mode Start/Stop semantics aren't visible in the window.
findings.evidence: r3.js toolbar() and strip() expanded header contain no Stop Feed; states 1.8/3.12 show Start Feed only when stopped; menubar rows 'Stop Feed'/'Stop Feeds'

findings.issue: Paused, no-signal and pending states are hand-built per page and diverge: paused ring orange on standalone vs no ring elsewhere; NEXT semantics differ (L10-07); the builder strip has no paused or failed branch.
findings.evidence: standalone/four-up/states page-local strips; r3.js strip() branches only rec / not recording

findings.issue: No 'confirm stop' or undo state exists for Stop Recording or Stop All in any component; Finishing begins immediately.
findings.evidence: states 1.3/1.5; menubar rows

findings.location: channel strip record row: 'Pause' + 'Stop' buttons; toolbar 'Stop'
findings.issue: 'Stop' means two different things one row apart: the strip's Stop ends the recording, the toolbar's Stop stops the feed (capture + camera output).
findings.evidence: main-expanded text: toolbar 'Stop' and strip 'Pause'/'Stop'; standalone also 'Stop All · 12:31', 'Stop All Recordings', 'Stop All Feeds', 'Stop Feeds' (menubar a)
findings.scenario: Mid-meeting the user wants to end the backup take, clicks the toolbar Stop and Zoom goes black; or ends the take when meaning to stop the feed.
findings.recommendation: Always name the object: never a bare 'Stop'.

rewrite.dropdown: Stop Feed / Stop All Feeds — one wording, not 'Stop Feeds'

alternatives: icon-only stop square with tooltip 'Stop Recording'

findings.issue: The main recording button has no verb on most pages; '12:31 · 2' reads as a status chip, not as 'click to stop both recordings'. Label differs per page.
findings.evidence: main-expanded '12:31 · 2'; four-up '12:31 · 3'; single '12:31'; standalone 'Stop All · 12:31'
findings.scenario: User clicks the red timer to see details and stops every take.
findings.recommendation: Verb first, status second, same pattern everywhere.
alternatives: split button: status chip + separate stop control

findings.location: 'In use by Zoom', 'ON AIR · Zoom', 'Program → Zoom', 'Live in Zoom', 'Zoom is waiting for video', 'Not in a meeting'
findings.issue: Copy names the consumer app and asserts 'meeting', but the app only knows whether its virtual camera has a client ('Virtual camera connected' in CaptureController). Naming Zoom (or 'not in a meeting') is a fabricated value under the honesty rule, and it isn't marked NEW.
findings.evidence: CaptureController.swift:640 'Virtual camera connected — choose Ultracam in Zoom'; no client-app lookup in Sources (CMIOExtensionClient.signingID is not used); standalone dropdown 'Not in a meeting'
findings.scenario: User sees 'ON AIR · Zoom' while FaceTime or OBS is the actual client, or 'Not in a meeting' while a browser meeting uses the camera.
findings.recommendation: Say what is known; add the app name only as a NEW feature backed by the extension reporting the client's signing ID.

rewrite.badge: ON AIR (no app name) or 'ON AIR · Zoom' marked NEW
rewrite.dropdown: Virtual cameras not in use (replace 'Not in a meeting')
rewrite.failed start: A camera app is waiting for video

alternatives: 'In use by zoom.us' from signing ID (NEW)

findings.location: picture badge 'ON AIR · Program' and strip 'On air in Program'
findings.issue: 'ON AIR' is used for the feed selected in Program regardless of whether Program itself has a consumer. Spec §5 defines On air (Program) as 'Program mode, selected feed'. 'On air' should mean someone is receiving it.
findings.evidence: spec.txt tally table: On air (Program) → 'Program mode, selected feed'
findings.scenario: Before Zoom opens the camera, the picture already says ON AIR; the user assumes they are visible.
findings.recommendation: Reserve 'ON AIR' for a consumed output; use 'PROGRAM' when selected but unwatched.

findings.issue: 'Live' (signal present, pipeline running) sits next to 'ON AIR' (being watched). In broadcast and meeting language these are synonyms, so a feed nobody is watching reads as live.
findings.evidence: main-expanded: 'Live · 2160p 59.94' on both strips; Feed 2 not on air
findings.scenario: Standalone recording: user thinks a 'Live' feed is being sent somewhere.
findings.recommendation: Describe the input, not 'live'.

findings.location: Program cut bar 'Feed 2 queued' vs picture 'NEXT' vs dropdown 'next' vs states 'CUTTING…'
findings.issue: One concept, three words (queued / next / cut pending). States distinguish director-next (green NEXT) from manual cut-pending (CUTTING…), but the cut bar uses 'queued' for the director's pick.
findings.evidence: program-view 'queued'; main-expanded 'NEXT'; menubar 'Feed 2 · next'; states 'CUTTING…'
findings.scenario: Operator can't tell if Feed 2 will cut automatically or if their own cut is pending.
findings.recommendation: Two terms only: 'Next' (director's choice) and 'Cutting…' (your cut waiting for a frame).

findings.location: noun for a source channel: 'Cameras' section, 'Add Camera', 'Remove Camera', '2 cameras' vs 'Feed 1', 'Stop Feed 2 to remove it', 'Backup · 2 feeds', 'Rename Feed 1…', 'Remove Feed 1'
findings.issue: 'Camera' means three things: the physical camera (FX3), the input channel (Feed 1), and the virtual camera (Ultracam · Feed 1). The same action is 'Remove Camera' in the popover and 'Remove Feed 1' in the Feed menu.
findings.evidence: main-collapsed popover 'Remove Camera' + 'Stop Feed 2 to remove it'; app-menus 'Remove Feed 1', 'Add Camera'; sidebar 'Cameras'; strip 'FX3 · Mini Recorder 12G'
findings.scenario: User removes 'Camera' expecting to drop the virtual camera from Zoom, or hunts for 'Feeds' in a list titled Cameras.
findings.recommendation: Feed = the input channel (all controls: Add Feed, Remove Feed, Feeds section). Camera = only the physical device and the published 'virtual camera'.

rewrite.menu: Add Feed / Rename Feed 1… / Remove Feed 1…

alternatives: call channels 'Camera 1/2' everywhere and the virtual camera 'Ultracam output'

findings.issue: One setting, four phrasings: 'Start with camera apps' (sidebar), 'Start When Camera Is in Use' (Feed menu), 'Start with Camera Apps' (dropdown), 'Start when camera is in use' (Settings, current app). Same for the NEW record option ('Record with camera apps' / 'Record when a camera app opens Ultracam').
findings.evidence: main-expanded sidebar; app-menus Feed; single dropdown; settings Camera/Recording
findings.scenario: User can't confirm the dropdown toggle and the sidebar switch are the same setting.
findings.recommendation: Keep the current app's wording and mirror it for recording.

rewrite.start: Start when camera is in use (menus: Start When Camera Is in Use)
rewrite.record: Record when camera is in use (menus: Record When Camera Is in Use)

findings.location: picture signal picker 'Output' / 'Source' / 'Source · S-Log3'; Settings & monitor-tools 'Processed Output'
findings.issue: 'Output' alone is ambiguous (output of what? to where?). Two names for the same option ('Output' vs 'Processed Output').
findings.evidence: main-expanded pill 'Output'; settings Monitor 'Source | Processed Output'; monitor-tools 'Output · as published · effects applied'
findings.scenario: User flips to 'Source' to check exposure, forgets, and later wonders why the picture looks flat while Zoom looks fine.
findings.recommendation: Use one pair everywhere; say which is which in the tooltip.

rewrite.tooltip: With Effects: what Program and the virtual camera receive. Camera Source: the HDMI input before effects. Doesn't change output or recordings.

alternatives: keep 'Output | Source' but rename Settings 'Processed Output' to 'Output'

findings.issue: 'clean source' is insider wording; the important fact (effects/LUT are not in the file) is implicit.
findings.evidence: strip row: 'ProRes 422 · clean source'; settings footnote explains it in full
findings.scenario: User applies a LUT for the meeting and is surprised the backup is flat S-Log3.
findings.recommendation: State it plainly in the strip; keep the long version in the tooltip.

rewrite.tooltip: Records the HDMI input as received: 2160p 10-bit 4:2:2 with embedded audio. LUT, scaling and color effects apply only to the virtual camera and Program.

findings.issue: The option named 'Source timecode' writes no timecode track (its own help says so). The name promises the camera's RP188 timecode in the file.
findings.evidence: RecordingModel.swift:33/41 title 'Source timecode', help 'No timecode track is written. Camera timecode still appears in the metadata panel…'
findings.scenario: Editor relies on camera TC for multicam sync; the files have none.
findings.recommendation: Rename to what it does (until source TC recording exists).

rewrite.modes: Mac Clock (default) · Start at 00:00:00:00 · No Timecode Track
rewrite.help for None: No timecode track is written. Camera timecode is shown live but not recorded.

alternatives: implement real source TC and keep the name

findings.issue: 'PC' is Windows vocabulary on a Mac app.
findings.evidence: settings 'PC time'; standalone status 'Timecode: PC time'; app-menus 'PC time'
findings.scenario: Minor confusion; looks unpolished.
findings.recommendation: Use Mac wording.

rewrite.label: Mac Clock
rewrite.help: Writes the Mac's clock as timecode, aligned to the first frame.

findings.issue: Same quantity written five ways: '00:12:31', '12:31', 'REC 12:31', 'Paused 04:12', '⏸ 4:12', 'Paused 4:12'. Leading zeros and hours appear inconsistently, so 1:02:47 vs 12:31 can be misread.
findings.evidence: strip '00:12:31'; picture 'REC 12:31'; standalone 'PAUSED 04:12' vs dropdown '⏸ 4:12' and 'Paused 4:12'
findings.scenario: Long recordings: '1:02' could be 1 h 2 m or 1 m 2 s.
findings.recommendation: h:mm:ss once ≥ 1 h, m:ss below; never mixed per screen.

rewrite.rule: 0:12:31 everywhere a take can exceed an hour (strip, toolbar, dropdown), REC 12:31 allowed only in compact pills

findings.scenario: Scanning two feeds side by side for a rate mismatch is slower than it should be.
findings.recommendation: Two forms only.

findings.issue: Bitrate units differ ('184 Mb/s' vs '10609.61 Mbps' vs '1.54 Mbps'); sample rate '48.0 kHz' vs '48 kHz'; a 10 Gb/s value printed as 10609.61 Mbps.
findings.evidence: strip '184 Mb/s'; diagnostics 'Video bitrate 10609.61 Mbps', 'Audio bitrate 1.54 Mbps'
findings.scenario: Hard to compare encoded vs captured bitrate.
findings.recommendation: One symbol, scaled.

rewrite.rule: Mb/s and Gb/s with 3 significant figures: 10.6 Gb/s, 184 Mb/s, 1.54 Mb/s; 48 kHz

findings.issue: 'Audio OK' summarizes two feeds as one; it hides a feed with no embedded audio and isn't a measured value.
findings.evidence: status bar segment 'Audio OK' on 2- and 4-feed pages
findings.scenario: Feed 2's HDMI audio is missing; the status bar still says OK.
findings.recommendation: Report per-feed facts; warn by name.

findings.issue: Glyph soup: 'REC 2 · ⏸ 1 · 12:31', 'Recording 1 of 2 · 21.5 GB' (means 1 recording + 1 paused, not 1 of 2 done).
findings.evidence: four-up status bar; standalone dropdown 'Recording 1 of 2'
findings.scenario: User reads '1 of 2' as one take failed.
findings.recommendation: Words for states, glyphs only as decoration.

findings.location: sidebar shot timer caption 'cut after 10 s' and 'Feed 1 · 8.2 s'
findings.issue: 'cut after 10 s' reads as a scheduled cut at 10 s; it's the minimum shot length (cut can happen any time after, at a speech gap). The dropdown uses a clearer 'Auto holds Feed 1 for 1.8 s more'.
findings.evidence: main-expanded sidebar; menubar a 'Auto holds Feed 1 for 1.8 s more'; program-view 'Cut to Feed 2 at the next speech gap after 10 s'
findings.scenario: Operator waits for a cut at 10 s that doesn't come.
findings.recommendation: Use the dropdown's phrasing everywhere.

rewrite.sidebar: Feed 1 · 8.2 s · can cut in 1.8 s

findings.issue: Popover action rows use sentence case ('Reset monitor tools', 'Copy monitor settings to') while the same commands are title case in menus; 'Diagnostics…' has an ellipsis but opens a window without asking for input; 'Feeds Program' is not a phrase.
findings.evidence: main-collapsed popover: 'Reset monitor tools', 'Copy monitor settings to', 'Diagnostics…', 'Feeds Program'; monitor-tools context menu 'Reset Monitor Tools'
findings.scenario: Inconsistent polish; 'Feeds Program' unreadable.
findings.recommendation: Title case for buttons/menu items; ellipsis only when more input follows.

rewrite.rows: Reset Monitor Tools · Copy Monitor Settings To ▸ · Show Diagnostics
rewrite.output row: Used in Program (Publish as Camera available in Separate mode)

findings.issue: Everyday surfaces leak internals: 'Without a producer frame for 0.5 s, the camera sends black'; 'matching source resolution and provenance are required'; 'GPU deadline exceeded'; 'writing final fragment'; 'sidecar'; 'counts as demand'.
findings.evidence: settings Camera footnote; monitor-tools Focus/Program captions; states 'Reduced monitoring · GPU deadline exceeded'; 'Finishing… writing final fragment'; timeline 'saved as a sidecar'
findings.scenario: User doesn't understand why focus peaking is greyed out on Program.
findings.recommendation: Plain language in UI, jargon only in Diagnostics.

rewrite.black frame: If Ultracam stops sending video for half a second, the camera app shows black.
rewrite.Program focus: Not available on Program: it switches between cameras, so there's no single source to analyze.
rewrite.reduced: Monitoring simplified to keep video smooth. Full quality returns automatically.
rewrite.sidecar: also saved as a timeline file next to the recordings

findings.issue: Error shown twice with different wording (banner 'Couldn't start Feed 1 — UltraStudio … is in use by another app' plus 'Zoom is waiting for video / Close the other app, then retry'); it asserts the cause (another app) although the SDK only reports the device busy/unavailable.
findings.evidence: menubar e; states 'Couldn't start · in use by another app'
findings.scenario: Device is actually unplugged; message sends the user hunting for another app.
findings.recommendation: One message: what failed, likely cause hedged, one action.

rewrite.banner: Couldn't start Feed 1. The UltraStudio is busy or unavailable — another app may be using it. [Retry]

findings.issue: 'Recording stopped after a source error.' gives no cause, no time, and no reassurance about what was saved.
findings.evidence: states 'Recording stopped after a source error.' (app's own RecordingModel message)
findings.scenario: After a cable glitch the user doesn't know whether the take is usable.
findings.recommendation: Cause (if known) + what's saved + action.

rewrite.message: Recording stopped at 0:12:31: the HDMI signal was lost. Everything up to then is saved. [Show in Finder] [Record Again]

findings.issue: Titles name modes the app doesn't have; the title would flip between 'Meeting' and 'Recording' as a client connects, which reads as a mode change.
findings.evidence: main-expanded 'Meeting'; four-up 'Recording Session'; standalone 'Recording'
findings.scenario: User looks for a Meeting/Recording mode switch that doesn't exist.
findings.recommendation: Stable title, state in subtitle.

findings.location: truncation of take names and paths
findings.issue: Take filenames truncate at the tail ('Feed 1_2026-10-20_08-…'), cutting the time and take number that distinguish takes; folders appear as breadcrumbs in strips ('Archive › B-cam') but raw paths in the popover ('/Volumes/Archive/B-cam').
findings.evidence: sidebar Recent Takes; popover Recording row
findings.scenario: Two takes from the same day look identical.
findings.recommendation: Human label first, truncate middle, one path style.

rewrite.take row: Today 08:02 · 38:12 (filename in tooltip, middle-truncated if shown)
rewrite.paths: Archive › B-cam everywhere; full path in tooltip

findings.issue: Several current-app help texts and states have no home in r3: 'Retry preview' + 'Restart preview rendering. Camera output continues.'; 'Applying change…'; Start disabled 'Waiting for the saved LUT to finish loading.'; 'Waiting for video' placeholder.
findings.evidence: grep of rendered r3 text: no 'Retry preview', 'Applying change', 'Waiting for the saved LUT', 'Waiting for video'
findings.scenario: Preview fails mid-meeting; there's no visible recovery text.
findings.recommendation: Add these strings to the states board and tooltips spec.

rewrite.preview error: Preview stopped. Camera output continues. [Retry Preview]

findings.issue: Settings panes and popovers carry multi-sentence footnotes (Monitor 'Under load' 3 sentences, Camera pane paragraph, Processing explanation) that belong in tooltips or Help.
findings.evidence: settings Monitor/Camera footnotes; main-collapsed Processing caption
findings.scenario: Dense panes; key controls harder to scan.
findings.recommendation: One short line max under a control; move the rest to .help and the Help book.

rewrite.Processing caption: Off: passes the camera signal through unchanged. ⇧⌘B

findings.problem: One click on a feed picture means cut (Program), focus the tile (monitor shortcuts) and implicitly select the feed. Adjusting zebra on Feed 2 mid-meeting cuts Zoom to Feed 2.
findings.evidence: main-expanded legend 2 ('Click a picture or press ⌃1/⌃2 to cut'); monitor-tools caption 'Click a tile to focus it (blue ring)'; MonitorWorkspaceShell.swift:77 TapGesture sets focusedTile; menubar (a) thumbnails 'click to cut'.

alternatives.name: A · Cut only from cut controls
alternatives.description: Picture click = focus/select only. Cuts happen from the toolbar cut group, the strip 'Cut to Feed N' button, ⌃1–⌃4 and the dropdown cut thumbnails (a dropdown click is deliberate). The tile shows a hover hint 'Cut ⌃2' instead of 'Click to cut'.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Safest and unambiguous. Cutting moves slightly away from the picture: one extra pointer move. Native: plain Buttons. Small build change.

alternatives.name: B · Double-click to cut
alternatives.description: Single click focuses; double-click cuts, with a 150 ms red flash on the ring as confirmation. Matches 'take' gestures in switcher software.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Fast, but a double-click by accident while focusing is still possible, and it's not discoverable or accessible without another path. It conflicts with any future double-click (e.g. expand tile).

alternatives.name: C · Click-to-cut only in Program view
alternatives.description: In Program view the source tiles are dedicated cut targets (no tools, no focus). In Side by Side the pictures never cut.
alternatives.tradeoffs: The mental model is clear per layout. Two behaviours for the same-looking tile is a mild inconsistency, and the default Side by Side then needs A's cut controls anyway.

findings.recommendation: A everywhere, plus C in Program view (source tiles there act as cut buttons, with no tools on them). Never let a picture click in Side by Side change the meeting.

findings.problem: The 'selected feed' still drives ⇧⌘B, the Feed menu, ⌘1–⌘4 and Load LUT ⌘O, but channel strips make all feeds peers and nothing shows which is selected. Bypass or Load LUT can hit the wrong camera live. Separate-mode Start/Stop also acts on the selected feed only, while Program mode starts all.
findings.evidence: app-menus Feed menu 'acts on Feed 1'; menubar (a) 'Processing · Feed 1'; AppModel.start()/stop() use selectedFeedID; no selection affordance in main-expanded / standalone.

alternatives.name: A · Focus = selection
alternatives.description: Merge the two concepts into one 'focused feed': accent focus ring on picture + strip header tint + sidebar row selection + window subtitle 'Feed 2'. Every feed command (⇧⌘B, ⌘O, Record ⌘R, Feed menu) acts on the focused feed, and menu items name it ('Bypass Feed 2'). ⌘1–⌘4 move focus.
alternatives.tradeoffs: One concept, always visible, matches today's 'shortcuts act on focused tile'. Needs the model's selectedFeedID wired to monitor focus. Low clutter.

alternatives.name: B · Feed-scoped commands only
alternatives.description: Drop the selected-feed idea from the UI. Per-feed actions live only in each strip and the ⋯ popover. Global commands become explicit ('Bypass All', 'Stop All Feeds'), and the Feed menu becomes submenus per feed (Feed 1 ›, Feed 2 ›) like the dropdown.
alternatives.tradeoffs: No hidden state. Loses fast keyboard toggles for one feed and makes the menu bar deeper. AppModel's selected-feed paths (preview renderer, LUT loader) still exist underneath.

alternatives.name: C · Keep selection, show it loudly
alternatives.description: Leave the model as is, but add a selected-state pill to the strip header ('Selected · ⇧⌘B acts here') and highlight the sidebar row.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Cheapest, but two near-identical ideas (focus vs selection) remain and users must learn the difference.

findings.recommendation: A. Also make Start/Stop explicit by scope: the toolbar says 'Stop All Feeds' in Program mode and 'Stop Feed 2' in Separate mode, and per-strip Stop Feed is always that feed.

findings.problem: Toggling Downscale, Color, Frame rate or Processing (bypass) while Zoom is connected renegotiates the output format (producer drains, renegotiates, resumes), which can blank or glitch the meeting. The UI presents these as harmless switches. The LUT toggle changes pixels only and is live-safe; the UI doesn't distinguish the two.
findings.evidence: README §Processing: 'The producer stops and drains its camera transport before negotiating a changed output format'; strip fx chips + processing switch in main-expanded/single; ⇧⌘B in dropdown.

alternatives.name: A · Inline live warning + confirm
alternatives.description: When a consumer is connected, format-changing toggles open a small popover: 'Changes the format Zoom receives (1080p → 2160p). Video pauses briefly.' [Change Now] [Cancel]. The LUT toggle stays instant. Chips get a tiny ⚠ glyph on hover while live.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Clear and native (confirmationDialog/popover). Adds one click only for the risky case. Copy must be precise.

alternatives.name: B · Meeting lock
alternatives.description: While any consumer is connected, a 'Live' lock state: format-changing controls are dimmed with 'Locked while Zoom is using this camera' and a lock button in the strip to unlock. LUT, cuts, recording and monitor tools stay available.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Strongest protection and less clutter during calls. Can frustrate the occasional intentional change. Needs a clear unlock path.

alternatives.name: C · Stage and apply
alternatives.description: Edits made while live are staged (chips outlined, 'Apply at next pause' / 'Apply now' bar).
alternatives.tradeoffs: Broadcast-like and safe, but it's an unfamiliar pattern for a desktop app and adds state to explain.

findings.recommendation: A by default, with B as a Settings option ('Lock format changes during meetings'). Label LUT as live-safe in the ⋯ popover.

findings.problem: Red means on air (Program or a consumer), REC, the record/stop button, errors, destructive actions and the Record All button. With two cameras, both pictures can show red rings or pills for different reasons, so the live operator can't read the state at a glance.
findings.evidence: main-expanded: red ring + red REC pill + red toolbar record button + red record buttons in strips; single: 'ON AIR · Zoom' red ring; states: error banners red; spec §2 'Red covers both on-air and REC'.

alternatives.name: A · Reserve red for ON AIR; REC becomes a glyph
alternatives.description: ON AIR keeps the red ring + filled badge. REC becomes a neutral glass pill with a small red dot and white text (no red fill anywhere else). Record buttons keep the standard red circle, a shape users already know. Errors move to orange/yellow with an exclamation triangle. The toolbar record control turns neutral-glass while rolling and shows '⏺ 12:31 · 2'.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Keeps convention: red tally means program. Red still appears in two meanings but with different shapes and sizes. Cheap CSS/builder change.

alternatives.name: B · Single status chip per picture
alternatives.description: One chip at top-left combines states: 'ON AIR · Zoom  •  ⏺ 12:31'. The ring alone shows the tally, and no separate REC pill sits bottom-right.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Least clutter, and one place to read. The chip grows long with two states; it needs truncation rules.

alternatives.name: C · Amber for recording
alternatives.description: Use a distinct hue (system orange) for REC, as some cameras do.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Clear separation, but it breaks the universal red REC convention and collides with paused/warning orange.

findings.recommendation: A + B: red ring = on air only, a single status chip per picture, REC dot glyph, errors orange with a triangle.

findings.problem: 'Stop' is ambiguous and unguarded. Toolbar Stop (feed), strip Stop (recording), Stop Feed (capture, which also ends recording), the record button turning into stop, and the toolbar '12:31 · 2' button (Stop All). Ending a take is one click next to Pause and can't be undone.
findings.evidence: main-expanded strip 'Pause' + 'Stop' adjacent; toolbar red '12:31 · 2'; AppModel.stop() calls recordingModel.stop(feedID:) so Stop Feed silently ends the take; four-up / standalone 'Stop All · 12:31'.

alternatives.name: A · Rename by object
alternatives.description: Capture: 'Start Feed / Stop Feed'. Recording: the record button toggles 'Record / End Take', and the strip has only Pause/Resume. Toolbar: 'End All Takes' as a menu-backed button (End All / Pause All). Stop Feed while recording reads 'Stop Feed and End Take'.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Clear verbs per object. Slightly longer labels. No new interaction.

alternatives.name: B · Guard the irreversible
alternatives.description: Ending a take longer than 1 minute, Stop Feed while recording or on air, and End All Takes ask once via a native confirmationDialog ('End Feed 1's take (12:31)?'), with 'Don't ask during meetings' off by default. Alternatively press-and-hold 0.6 s on the record button with a ring fill.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Prevents the costly mistake. Adds a click; press-and-hold is less discoverable and needs an accessibility alternative.

alternatives.name: C · Spatial separation
alternatives.description: Keep Pause inline. Move End Take to the record button only (far right) and Stop Feed into the strip header ⋯ menu.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Reduces misclicks without dialogs. Stop Feed becomes less reachable.

findings.recommendation: A + B (confirm only when the action ends a recording or interrupts an on-air feed) + C (Stop Feed into ⋯ when recording).

findings.problem: Each live state is repeated across 5–6 surfaces (sidebar camera rows, strip, picture pill, toolbar, status bar, menu bar icon), and the picture keeps 5 tool buttons visible at all times. With 1–2 cameras the sidebar camera list duplicates the strips: the clutter the user asked to remove.
findings.evidence: main-expanded: 'REC 12:31' appears in sidebar rows, sidebar Recording, picture pill, strip, toolbar, status bar; sidebar Cameras rows mirror strips; always-on tool groups on 524 px pictures.

alternatives.name: A · One job per surface
alternatives.description: Picture = live state (status chip + tally). Strip = per-feed controls and numbers. Sidebar = session totals only (no per-feed rows when ≤2 cameras; output, destination, takes, automation). Status bar = global summary + problems. Menu bar icon = global state. Document it in the spec.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Big clutter reduction with no loss. The sidebar becomes lighter (could be narrower, ~200 pt). With 3–4 cameras, a compact camera list can return.

alternatives.name: B · Hover-only overlays with pinned tools
alternatives.description: Tool buttons and the hover group appear on pointer hover or focus. Tools that are on show as small passive chips ('Zebra 95', 'Guides') that stay visible.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Clean pictures. Discoverability is slightly lower (mitigated by the View › Monitor Tools menu and a first-run hint). It needs keyboard focus to reveal them for accessibility.

alternatives.name: C · Density setting
alternatives.description: Comfortable vs Compact in Settings › General, affecting overlays, strips and the sidebar.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Lets users choose, but it's a setting instead of a decision, and it doubles design states.

findings.recommendation: A + B; skip C.

findings.problem: The hybrid dropdown runs 20–26 rows plus a 180 pt preview (and cut thumbnails), exceeding a 13" laptop's usable height. Submenus nest three deep (Feed › Effects ›), and it's partly a duplicate menu bar.
findings.evidence: menubar (a): preview + thumbnails + ~22 rows + stat line; single dropdown ~24 rows; app-menus duplicates most rows.

alternatives.name: A · Control-surface top + short menu
alternatives.description: Preview (shrinks first on small screens), then a row of 4 glass buttons (Feed Start/Stop, Record/End All, Effects/Bypass, Auto). Then per-feed rows with submenus. Then Open Ultracam / Settings / Quit. Target ≤ 12 rows; the rest stays in app menus.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Fast and graphical. The custom button row needs the NSMenu custom-view spike (same as the preview). Less 'native menu' feel at the top.

alternatives.name: B · State-contextual rows
alternatives.description: Show only rows that apply now: Program rows only in Program mode, recording rows only when a folder exists or a take is rolling, automation rows hidden when unchanged. A 'More' submenu holds the rest.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Shorter menus, but rows move between states, which hurts muscle memory.

alternatives.name: C · Compact preview mode
alternatives.description: Preview collapses to a 64 pt strip with chips (ON AIR, REC, TC) when the screen is shorter than 900 pt, or via a toggle.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Solves height only, not length.

findings.recommendation: A with C's adaptive preview height. Keep row order stable (avoid B).

findings.problem: First run depends on activating the camera system extension (signed build, System Settings approval, possibly pending) before Zoom sees anything. The design covers this only as scattered banners and one onboarding card, with no persistent progress or live approval status.
findings.evidence: states §6 'First launch' card; sidebar banner 'Install the Ultracam camera'; ExtensionInstaller status/pending; README install section (approve in System Settings › Login Items & Extensions).

alternatives.name: A · Setup checklist that docks into the sidebar
alternatives.description: First launch shows a checklist card in the main area: Install camera (live status: requested → waiting for approval → enabled, with an 'Open System Settings' button), Choose input (live signal check), Optional LUT, Recording folder, Test in Zoom. After first completion it collapses to a 'Setup 3/5' sidebar row and disappears when done.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Guides without blocking: preview and recording work during setup. Small new component.

alternatives.name: B · Modal onboarding sheet
alternatives.description: A multi-step sheet before the window is usable.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Linear and clear, but it blocks monitoring and recording, and most of the steps are optional.

alternatives.name: C · Empty states only
alternatives.description: Each surface explains itself when empty.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Zero new UI, but there's no overview of what's left, and approval in System Settings is easy to miss.

findings.recommendation: A.

findings.location: Strip Processing switch, effect chips (1080p, 4:2:0, 29.97), ⇧⌘B in Feed menu and dropdown, ⋯ popover Processing section
findings.issue: Effect and bypass changes that alter the output format interrupt the Zoom feed, but every surface presents them as harmless one-click toggles with no warning, confirmation or deferral.
findings.evidence: CaptureController.reconfigure() resets the sample factory and sets message 'Updating output…'; CameraSink.send() throws 'Frame does not match the virtual camera's negotiated format and timing' on a size/pixel-format/duration change; CaptureController then disconnects the camera, schedules a reconnect after cameraRetryInterval and counts an outage. The extension emits black after 0.5 s without a producer frame (README). README: 'consumers must accept the selected format'. Downscale, Color, Frame rate and Processing (bypass = 2160p x422) all change the format; LUT alone does not.
findings.scenario: Mid-call the user presses ⇧⌘B or clicks the 1080p chip to compare. Zoom's picture goes black or freezes during the reconnect, or never recovers if Zoom rejects 2160p 10-bit 4:2:2.
findings.recommendation: Classify every control as live-safe or disruptive. When the feed's camera is in use (or it's on air in Program), disruptive changes show an inline confirmation ('Changes the format Zoom receives; the picture blanks for about a second') or are staged as 'Apply at next stop'. LUT stays instant. Chips become read-only summaries while the camera is in use; editing moves to the ⋯ popover with the warning.
alternatives: 'Pending changes · Apply' bar that applies all format changes in one renegotiation
Meeting lock: format-changing controls disabled while a consumer is connected, with an explicit Unlock
Hold-to-toggle for chips while live
affects: states (new 'Updating output…' and 'Change will interrupt Zoom' states)
findings.verified: CameraSink.swift:434-450 throws on negotiated format mismatch

findings.location: Feed picture click; dropdown cut thumbnails
findings.issue: A single click on a feed picture is defined as 'cut Program to this feed', while monitor-tools defines the same click as 'focus this tile' (and focus also drives ⌃⌥F/⌃⌥C and likely the selected feed). One gesture has three meanings, one of them visible in the meeting.
findings.evidence: main-expanded legend 2: 'Click a picture or press ⌃1/⌃2 to cut.' program-view: 'Click a source to cut.' monitor-tools: 'Click a tile to focus it (blue ring). Shortcuts act on the focused tile only, as today.' Current code: MonitorWorkspaceShell surface() uses TapGesture to set focusedTile. menubar (a): 'Click a camera to cut'.
findings.scenario: During a Program meeting the user clicks Feed 2's picture to turn on zebra or freeze it; Zoom immediately cuts to Feed 2. In the dropdown, a click meant to open the menu row lands on a thumbnail and cuts.
findings.recommendation: Picture click only focuses/selects. Cuts happen from explicit cut controls (toolbar cut buttons, strip 'Cut to Feed N', ⌃n) or a deliberate gesture. In the dropdown, thumbnails show tally only; cuts are menu items ('Cut to Feed 2 ⌃2').
alternatives: Double-click a picture to cut
⌥-click to cut, with a hover hint
Click arms the cut (green 'Take' button appears), second click or Return takes it (preview/program 'Take' model)

findings.location: Stop Feed / Stop Feeds ⌘↩ (dropdown, Feed menu), ⋯ popover
findings.issue: Stopping a feed also ends its recording and its Zoom output, but every Stop Feed control is a plain one-key/one-click action with no mention of either consequence.
findings.evidence: AppModel.stop(): manuallyStoppedFeeds.insert, feedCoordinator.stop(selectedFeedID), recordingModel.stop(feedID: selectedFeedID). Recording also stops on any stopped capture update (AppModel onUpdate: update.stopped → recordingModel.stop). Pages: menubar 'Stop Feed ⌘↩' and 'Stop Feeds ⌘↩' rows next to Processing; app-menus Feed 'Stop Feed ⌘↩'. No page states that it ends the take.
findings.scenario: The user means to stop recording, picks 'Stop Feed' (top row of the dropdown, highlighted position) or presses ⌘↩ with Ultracam frontmost. Zoom goes black and the backup take finalizes.
findings.recommendation: When the feed is recording or its camera is in use, Stop Feed asks first: 'Stop Feed 1? Zoom loses the camera and the recording (12:31) is finished.' [Stop Feed] [Cancel]. Move Stop Feed below the recording rows in the dropdown; keep ⌘↩ but route it through the same confirmation when anything is live.
alternatives: Disable Stop Feed while recording ('Stop the recording first')
Undo-style 5 s grace: 'Stopping Feed 1… Undo' before teardown
Hold ⌘↩ for 1 s while live

findings.location: Expanded strip Pause | Stop buttons; record button turning into stop; collapsed strip record button next to ⋯
findings.issue: Ending a take is a single unguarded click on a control that sits beside Pause (same size and style) or beside ⋯ (9 pt gap) and shares its target with Record. A finished take can't be resumed; it becomes a new file.
findings.evidence: r3.js strip(): Pause and Stop as adjacent identical .btn (24 pt), plus the 30 pt recbtn that is 'on' (= stop) while recording. Collapsed strip: recbtn sm (30 pt) then btn icon ⋯ (24 pt) with 9 pt gap. main-collapsed hover row adds Pause/Stop inline. RecordingModel.stop finalizes the movie.
findings.scenario: Reaching for ⋯ on a collapsed strip during a meeting, or for Pause, the user clicks Stop; the backup take ends and the next segment is a separate file (or nothing, if they don't notice).
findings.recommendation: One primary record control per strip: red Record → while recording becomes a square Stop that needs confirmation or a 1 s press-and-hold (with a progress ring), Pause stays a separate, visually secondary control placed away from Stop. Collapsed strips show state only; stop lives in hover controls with spacing ≥ 16 pt from ⋯.
alternatives: Stop asks only if the take is longer than 1 min
'Take ended · Resume as new take' toast with one click

findings.issue: The most prominent control in the window is a Stop All button whose label is elapsed time, not an action. One click finalizes every recording, and its look is identical to the Record All button it replaces.
findings.evidence: r3.js toolbar(): tb-prominent red with stop icon and recLabel ('12:31 · 2'); main-expanded legend 5 calls it 'Record All shows elapsed time and the number of takes'. standalone uses 'Stop All · 12:31'. ⌥⌘R toggles Record All / Stop All (app-menus).
findings.scenario: The user glances at the timer and clicks it expecting details; both backup takes stop. Pressing ⌥⌘R twice (once to check) starts new takes.
findings.recommendation: Split status from action: the toolbar shows a REC status chip (elapsed, count) that opens the recording popover; Stop All lives in that popover and the Record menu with a confirmation listing the takes. Use separate shortcuts for Record All and Stop All, or make ⌥⌘R start-only.
alternatives: Keep the button but label it 'Stop All' with elapsed as secondary text, plus confirmation when > 1 take
Hold-to-stop on the toolbar button

findings.issue: Keyboard and menu commands act on an invisible 'selected feed'. With strips making all feeds equal, the user can't see which camera ⇧⌘B or Stop Feed ⌘↩ will hit.
findings.evidence: AppModel: pipelineEnabled, start(), stop(), chooseLUT() all target selectedFeedID. app-menus: Feed menu header 'acts on Feed 1'; menubar labels the Processing row 'Feed 1' only in Program state. main-expanded shows no selection marker (sidebar row 1 has a subtle fill, ambiguous with tally).
findings.scenario: Two-camera meeting: the user clicked Feed 2's strip earlier, then presses ⇧⌘B intending Feed 1. Feed 2 (on air) bypasses, changing format mid-call (see L2-01).
findings.recommendation: Either show selection unmistakably (selected strip/picture gets an accent outline distinct from tally; menu items name the feed: 'Bypass Feed 2 ⇧⌘B') or remove the global commands and make every command feed-scoped (Feed ▸ Feed 1 ▸ …, strip ⋯). Never let a disruptive shortcut target a feed whose name isn't in the command.
alternatives: Selection follows the focused tile only, with the name echoed in the toolbar title
Disruptive global shortcuts disabled when > 1 feed is live

findings.location: Program-mode 'Stop Feeds ⌘↩' (dropdown a), toolbar/Feed menu Stop
findings.issue: In Program mode Start starts every source, but Stop only stops the selected feed (and its recording). The dropdown's 'Stop Feeds' label promises the opposite.
findings.evidence: AppModel.startFeed(): in .program starts every enabled descriptor with a device. AppModel.stop(): feedCoordinator.stop(selectedFeedID) and recordingModel.stop(feedID: selectedFeedID) only; other headless sources keep running and recording. menubar (a): 'Stop Feeds ⌘↩'.
findings.scenario: After the meeting the user chooses 'Stop Feeds' believing everything stopped; Feed 2 keeps capturing and recording to disk.
findings.recommendation: Make the label match the behavior per mode ('Stop Feed 1' vs 'Stop All Feeds'), and design an explicit 'Stop All Feeds' (ending all takes, with confirmation). Flag the start/stop asymmetry for the runtime (L8).
alternatives: End Session command: stops all feeds and takes and lists what was saved

findings.location: Manual cut while Auto is on
findings.issue: Manual cuts while Auto switching is on are sent to the director as a manual override, but no page shows what happens next (does Auto hold, cut back, or turn off?). The operator can't predict whether their cut will stick.
findings.evidence: AppModel.requestProgramCut → autoSwitcherBridge.manualOverride(cameraID:at:); NaturalTalkingHeadSettings has manualHold. states shows 'Auto holding' (shot timer) and 'Auto off · manual', but no 'Manual override · Auto resumes in …' state; toolbar cut buttons sit next to the Auto toggle with no hint.
findings.scenario: The user cuts to Feed 2 for a demo; 3 s later Auto cuts back to Feed 1 mid-sentence.
findings.recommendation: Design a 'Manual hold' state: after a manual cut with Auto on, show 'Held on Feed 2 · Auto resumes after the shot timer / Resume Auto now', and decide (with the director's real behavior) whether Auto pauses until resumed. Show it on the tally badge, sidebar Program section and dropdown.
alternatives: Manual cut turns Auto off (explicit, simplest)
Setting: 'Manual cuts pause Auto' (maps to manualHold)

findings.location: ⌃1–⌃4 cut vs ⌘1–⌘4 select feed vs ⌥⌘1–⌥⌘4 layout; ⌘R record/stop selected
findings.issue: Three families of number shortcuts differ only by modifier, and the one that changes the meeting (⌃n cut) is the easiest to hit by mistake. ⌘R (proposed record/stop) is 'reload' muscle memory elsewhere, and it can stop a take.
findings.evidence: app-menus shortcut table: ⌃1–⌃4 Cut (proposed), ⌘1–⌘4 Select feed, ⌥⌘1–⌥⌘4 Layout, ⌘R Record/Stop selected feed. spec §6 lists the same.
findings.scenario: The user means ⌘2 (select Feed 2 to adjust it) and presses ⌃2: Zoom cuts. Or presses ⌘R expecting a refresh and stops the recording.
findings.recommendation: Make ⌘R start-only (never stop), and stop via a confirmed command. Keep cut shortcuts but give them visible feedback (tally flash + 'Cut to Feed 2 · ⌘Z-like Undo cut' for 3 s, which cuts back). Consider dropping ⌘1–⌘4 select if selection is removed (L2-06).
alternatives: Cuts on plain 1–4 only in Program view
Require Return to take an armed cut

findings.issue: The quit sheet covers recordings only. Quitting while a meeting app is using Ultracam's camera cuts the meeting's video with no warning.
findings.evidence: states 'Quit while recording': 'Quit stops capture and waits for active takes to finish.' AppDelegate.applicationShouldTerminate only defers for active recordings. Settings General: 'Quit waits for active recordings to finish.' No state for 'camera in use by Zoom'.
findings.scenario: The user quits Ultracam from the dropdown during a call to tidy the menu bar; Zoom's video goes black.
findings.recommendation: When any virtual camera is in use, ⌘Q shows 'Zoom is using Ultracam · Quitting stops the camera in the meeting' [Quit] [Cancel], combined with the recording summary if takes are active. Offer 'Close Window' as the default for users who just want it out of the way.
alternatives: Quit becomes 'Hide' while a consumer is connected unless ⌥ is held

findings.issue: The brief output interruption after a configuration change (and the camera reconnect after a transport error) has no design. The current app's 'Applying change…' and 'Updating output…' messages and the camera-outage state are missing from every page, so after a disruptive change the user can't tell whether Zoom is getting a picture.
findings.evidence: CaptureController.reconfigure sets message 'Updating output…'; on send failure cameraMessage 'Camera output disconnected — …' and a timed reconnect. Inventory §2.1 'Applying change…'. grep finds no 'Updating output', 'Applying change' or reconnect state in r3 pages.
findings.scenario: After toggling Downscale, Zoom shows black for a second; the Ultracam picture still looks live, so the user assumes it's Zoom's fault, or toggles again (another renegotiation).
findings.recommendation: Add an output-health state to the tally/output row: 'Updating output…' (spinner) → 'Reconnecting to Zoom…' (orange) → normal. Show it on the picture badge, the strip output row, the status bar output segment and the dropdown.
alternatives: Toast 'Zoom output paused for 0.8 s' after each renegotiation

findings.location: Failure mid-take: HDMI lost, destination drive disconnected
findings.issue: Mid-take failures that matter most for a backup recorder are not designed: HDMI signal loss while recording (detection stays armed, so the take continues with no frames, or ends), and the recording drive being unplugged. Only 'disk low' and 'dropped frames' exist.
findings.evidence: CaptureController watchdog: with startAutomatic, signal loss → 'No video signal — waiting for HDMI.' (capture not stopped). RecordingModel: 'Recording stopped after a source error.' states covers No signal (not recording), Failed, disk low; four-up Feed 3 'No signal' is idle. No 'signal lost while recording' or 'drive disconnected' card.
findings.scenario: The camera's HDMI cable is bumped 20 minutes into a meeting; the user doesn't know whether the backup has a gap, stopped, or resumed.
