findings.recommendation: Design 'Signal lost · recording continues (gap 00:03)' vs 'Recording stopped: signal lost · Start new take' depending on actual recorder behavior (verify), and 'Drive disconnected · take saved up to 12:31 (recoverable)'. Make both visible on the strip, picture, status bar and menu bar icon (attention dot).
alternatives: Auto-start a new take when the signal returns (proposal, NEW)

findings.issue: Recover is offered during an active recording. Recovery copies complete fragments of a large interrupted movie, likely to the same drive the live takes are writing to, which risks I/O contention and dropped frames in the live take.
findings.evidence: README: 'Recovery copies complete fragments into a separate _Recovered.mov without re-encoding'. r3 sidebar shows 'Interrupted · Recover' while 'Backup · 2 feeds 12:31' is recording on the same 8TB drive.
findings.scenario: During a meeting the user clicks Recover on yesterday's take; a multi-GB copy runs on the 8TB drive and today's takes start dropping frames.
findings.recommendation: While any take is recording, Recover is disabled with 'Available when recordings stop', or it asks first ('Recovery copies 41 GB on 8TB while recording; this may cause dropped frames').
alternatives: Queue the recovery to run automatically after recording stops

findings.location: NEW 'Record with camera apps' + 'Stop when the last camera app closes'
findings.issue: The proposed auto-stop can end a recording the user started deliberately (standalone) when an unrelated camera client closes, for example Zoom's settings preview.
findings.evidence: settings Recording/Automation: 'Stop when the last camera app closes' (NEW) with no scope. README: 'Zoom's camera settings preview also counts as camera use.' Current code keeps feeds running while recording (reconcileAutomaticFeed guard !recording), so this would be new behavior.
findings.scenario: The user records a standalone interview, opens Zoom to check something, and closes it; auto-stop finalizes the interview take.
findings.recommendation: Scope auto-stop to takes that auto-record started ('Stop backup takes it started'); manually started takes are never auto-stopped. Show the origin on the strip ('Backup · started with Zoom').
alternatives: Grace period: auto-stop after 30 s without a client, with 'Keep Recording' in a notification

findings.location: Toolbar cut buttons next to Auto toggle; layout picker and collapse toggle in the same toolbar row
findings.issue: Meeting-affecting controls (cuts) sit in the same glass row as view-only controls (layout, collapse strips), styled alike, with no separation. Mis-clicks between a view change and a cut are likely, and view controls don't read as safe.
findings.evidence: r3.js toolbar(): cuts group (Feed 1 red / Feed 2 green outline / Auto) directly followed by the layout group and the collapse toggle; same tb-group glass style and height.
findings.scenario: Reaching for Side by Side, the user clicks the 'Feed 2' cut pill.
findings.recommendation: Group live controls (cut, Auto, Record) on the trailing side behind a ToolbarSpacer, and view controls (layout, collapse, sidebar) leading or in the View menu. Make view controls visually quieter.
alternatives: Move cut buttons into a dedicated cut bar only in Program view and the strips

findings.location: Sleep / lid close / display sleep while live
findings.issue: Nothing tells the user that closing the lid or system sleep will stop the meeting feed and recordings. The app prevents idle sleep while capturing, but that's invisible.
findings.evidence: CaptureController begins ProcessInfo activity [.userInitiated, .latencyCritical] ('Live UltraStudio video processing'), which prevents idle sleep only. No page covers sleep or lid close.
findings.scenario: The user closes a laptop lid for a moment during a recording break; capture and the take stop.
findings.recommendation: Status bar/Info note 'Preventing idle sleep while live'. After wake, a strip state explains what was interrupted ('Stopped by sleep at 14:22 · take saved').

findings.issue: There's no single way to protect a live session. Every disruptive control (bypass, effects, stop feed, stop take, cut by click, input/LUT changes) is always armed, and the fixes above have to be applied piecemeal.
findings.evidence: Aggregate of L2-01..L2-06; no lock or meeting mode on any page.
findings.scenario: A presenter wants to hand off the laptop or present from it without risking the stream.
findings.recommendation: Propose (NEW) 'Live Lock' (toolbar padlock, ⌃⌘L): while on, disruptive controls need confirmation or are disabled; cut, record and Auto stay available. It turns on automatically when a camera client connects (setting). Pair with the per-control rules above rather than replacing them.
alternatives: No global mode; rely on per-control guards (L2-01, -03, -04, -05)

findings.issue: A single click on a feed picture is defined as cut-to-Program, focus-tile and (implicitly) select-feed at the same time.
findings.evidence: main-expanded legend 2 'Click a picture or press ⌃1/⌃2 to cut'; monitor-tools 'Click a tile to focus it (blue ring). Shortcuts act on the focused tile'; current code MonitorWorkspaceShell surface() TapGesture sets focusedTile; app-menus 'Feed acts on Feed 1' (selected).
findings.scenario: Mid-meeting the user clicks Feed 2 to open its zebra settings or freeze it; Zoom cuts to Feed 2.
findings.recommendation: Picture click = focus/select only. Cut only from explicit cut controls (toolbar cut buttons, strip 'Cut to Feed N', ⌃n, dropdown thumbnails).
alternatives: double-click picture to cut
⌥-click to cut
setting 'Click picture to cut' off by default
affects: menubar (thumbnails are fine: dedicated cut surface)

findings.issue: The 'selected feed' (target of ⇧⌘B, Feed menu, ⌘R, ⌘O) has no visible indicator and is conflated with tile focus: spec calls ⌘1–⌘4 'Focus feed (keyboard target)' while app-menus calls the same keys 'Select Feed'.
findings.evidence: Only cue is an unlabeled highlighted first row in sidebar() Cameras (r3.js i===0 background); hidden entirely when the sidebar is hidden (four-up). spec.html §6 '⌘1–⌘4 Focus feed (keyboard target)' vs app-menus.html 'Select Feed ⌘1'. AppModel.selectedFeedID drives pipelineEnabled/configuration/LUT/start().
findings.scenario: User presses ⇧⌘B intending to bypass Feed 2 (the picture they last looked at) and bypasses Feed 1, which is on air.
findings.recommendation: Make focus and selection one concept ('focused feed'), shown with an accent outline on picture+strip header distinct from tally, and name the target in menu items ('Bypass Feed 1  ⇧⌘B').
alternatives: remove the selected concept: all per-feed commands live on strips; menu items become submenus per feed

findings.issue: Every strip shows live per-feed state (timecode, audio meters, format, processing switch, effect chips, LUT) for all feeds at once, but AppModel only publishes and edits the selected feed.
findings.evidence: AppModel installCaptureUpdateHandler: 'guard self.selectedFeedID == feedID else { return }' drops updates for other feeds; configuration, pipelineEnabled, lut*, previewEnabled, automaticFeedEnabled are single properties bound to selectedFeedID; non-selected Program sources run headless with Apply LUT off until restoreHeadlessLUT.
findings.scenario: Feed 2's strip shows frozen or empty meters/TC, and toggling its LUT chip actually edits Feed 1 unless selection silently switches first.
findings.recommendation: Treat the strip as the source of truth and add a per-feed observable model (e.g. FeedState keyed by FeedID: update, configuration, pipelineEnabled, LUT, preview, automatic). Note it in spec §4 as a required model change.
alternatives: interaction auto-selects the feed before editing (rebinds main native preview; flicker risk)

findings.issue: No visible Start/Stop Feed control exists in the main window on 5 of 6 window pages; the r3 toolbar() and expanded strip() header dropped it. It is reachable only via ⌘↩, the Feed menu or the dropdown.
findings.evidence: grep: 'Stop Feed' absent from main-expanded, main-collapsed, program-view, standalone, four-up (present only in single.html and states 'Feed stopped' strip). r3.js toolbar() has cuts/layout/collapse/record only. Current app's primary control is StartStopButton.
findings.scenario: User wants to stop capture after a meeting (or restart a misbehaving feed) and can't find the control in the window.
findings.recommendation: Add a per-feed capture control to the strip header (the 'Live · 2160p' badge becomes a Live/Stopped menu button) and a toolbar Start/Stop (Program mode: all sources, labeled 'Stop All Feeds').
alternatives: only in ⋯ popover footer (too hidden)

findings.issue: Recording state for the same takes is printed in 7 places at once with no hierarchy: sidebar camera rows, sidebar Recording section, picture REC pill, strip 'RECORDING 00:12:31', toolbar '12:31 · 2', status bar 'REC 2 feeds 12:31', menu bar icon dot.
findings.evidence: main-expanded render; r3.js sidebar() camRows 'REC ${t}', sidebar Recording row, tile() rec pill, strip(), toolbar recLabel, statusbar().
findings.scenario: Visual noise competes with the one thing that must stand out (on-air), and a single failing take is hard to spot among identical timers.
findings.recommendation: Primary = strip (per feed, with controls). On-picture echo = small REC pill. Aggregate control = toolbar Record All. Status bar summary only when the sidebar is hidden. Remove per-camera REC text from sidebar rows; menu bar dot stays.
alternatives: sidebar Recording section as the only aggregate and drop status bar REC

findings.issue: The expanded strip has two stop-recording controls side by side (the record button in its stop state and a 'Stop' button) next to Pause, and 'Stop' means stop recording here but stop capture in 'Stop Feed(s)' elsewhere.
findings.evidence: r3.js strip(): recBtn 'recbtn on' + 'PauseStop'; menubar 'Stop Feed ⌘↩' vs strip 'Stop'.
findings.scenario: User aims for Pause and hits Stop (or the record button), ending the take.
findings.recommendation: One record control per feed (record ↔ stop, labeled 'Stop Recording' in its tooltip/accessibility), Pause as a separate secondary button; reserve 'Stop' wording for recording and rename capture to 'Turn Off Feed'/'Stop Capture'.
alternatives: keep Stop button, make record button record-only (disabled while recording)

findings.issue: Auto switching has two or three live toggles on one screen (toolbar 'Auto', sidebar 'Auto switching' switch, Program view cut bar 'Auto') and strategy has two pop-ups (sidebar + cut bar).
findings.evidence: r3.js toolbar() cuts group 'Auto'; sidebar() program output 'Auto switching' switch + strategy popup; program-view.html lines 68–69 Auto + strategy in cut bar.
findings.scenario: Two controls for one setting suggests they differ; the user isn't sure which one is authoritative.
findings.recommendation: Toolbar owns cut + Auto. Sidebar Output shows Program status read-only (on-air feed, shot timer, strategy as text that opens the Program menu). Program view cut bar replaces the toolbar group instead of adding to it.
alternatives: sidebar owns Auto/strategy, toolbar only cuts

findings.issue: The design names the consuming app ('In use by Zoom', 'ON AIR · Zoom', 'Ultracam · Program → Zoom') but the app only knows a boolean demand per virtual camera route; no client identity exists.
findings.evidence: CameraDemandMonitor: CameraDemandChange { route, requested: Bool?, error } — no app name; current UI says 'Camera connected'. r3.js statusbar '→ ${consumer}', tile consumer badge.
findings.scenario: With Zoom and Teams both open, or Photo Booth previewing, the UI states something it can't know.
findings.recommendation: Use 'In use' / 'ON AIR · In use' unless app identity becomes available; list consumer naming as an explicit NEW proposal needing a feasibility check.
alternatives: show 'In use by a camera app' with count if multiple routes

findings.issue: Automation is presented as two global session switches in the sidebar, but automatic start is stored per feed, and the NEW 'Record with camera apps' has no defined scope in Separate mode.
findings.evidence: FeedDescriptor.automaticFeed; AppModel.startFeed checks descriptor.automaticFeed for other sources; settings.html Camera 'Default for new cameras · each camera can override'; r3.js sidebar() 'Start with camera apps' single switch.
findings.scenario: User turns 'Start with camera apps' off in the sidebar expecting all cameras to stop auto-starting; Feed 2 still starts when its camera opens.
findings.recommendation: Per-feed control in the ⋯ popover, a default in Settings, and a sidebar summary ('Auto start: 2 of 2'). Define Record-with-camera-apps: Separate = the feed whose camera is in use; Program = all enabled sources.

findings.issue: With 1–2 cameras the sidebar Cameras list repeats what the strips already show (name, format, REC, tally dot), the redundancy the user rejected in round 2.
findings.evidence: r3.js sidebar() camRows render every feed; strips directly beside show the same fields.
findings.scenario: Space the user explicitly asked not to waste.
findings.recommendation: Show only cameras not visible in the current layout (e.g. Single layout with 2 feeds), plus 'Add Camera'; otherwise a one-line summary ('2 cameras · both live').
alternatives: keep list only in Four Up/Program view where pictures are small

findings.issue: When the sidebar is visible, the status bar repeats its output→consumer, recording and disk information; their jobs overlap.
findings.evidence: statusbar() segments: output→consumer, Program on air, REC + time left; sidebar() Output, Recording, disk gauge.
findings.scenario: Two summaries of the same thing push out warnings and resources.
findings.recommendation: Status bar = warnings + resources + timecode mode when the sidebar is visible; full session summary only when the sidebar is hidden.
alternatives: keep status bar constant and slim the sidebar instead

findings.issue: The master Processing switch in the strip is an unlabeled toggle after the effect chips, and the applied-state feedback ('Applying change…', 'Effects active', 'Complete bypass active') from the current app appears on no r3 page.
findings.evidence:
r3.js strip(): `${fxChips(f)}
` with no label; grep 'Applying change' → no r3 matches; inventory §2.1 AppliedPipelineState.
findings.scenario: User flips a green switch not knowing it bypasses everything, then can't tell whether the change has reached Zoom yet.
findings.recommendation: Label it 'Processing' in the expanded strip with applied-state text (Effects active / Applying… / Complete bypass); collapsed strip shows a 'Bypass' badge when off.

findings.issue: The menu bar icon encodes one feed's processing/bypass state (video.fill vs arrow.right.square) but the session has up to 4 feeds with independent processing; mixed states are undefined.
findings.evidence: menubar.html icon strip; current MenuBarStatusIcon uses model.update.pipelineEnabledApplied (selected feed only).
findings.scenario: Feed 1 processing, Feed 2 bypassed: the icon shows whichever feed is selected.
findings.recommendation: Icon priority: attention > recording > live (any published feed) > waiting > stopped; drop the bypass glyph from the icon and show bypass in the dropdown.

findings.issue: The same sidebar dot changes meaning by mode: green = next in Program mode but live in Separate mode; orange = paused, skipped-by-Auto or warning.
findings.evidence: r3.js sidebar(): program mode i===0 red / else green; separate mode all green; standalone/states use orange for paused and skipped.
findings.scenario: Switching modes silently changes what the colors mean.
findings.recommendation: Sidebar dot = recording/health only; tally role as text ('On air', 'Next') where needed.

findings.issue: 'Drops' refers to two different counters without saying which: recording dropped video frames (strip '0 dropped') and capture/pipeline drops ('Delivered 29.97 fps · 0 drops', diagnostics stages).
findings.evidence: r3.js strip uses f.rec.drops (RecordingStatistics.droppedVideoFrames); single.html signal path 'Delivered … 0 drops' (CaptureUpdate.videoDrops); diagnostics 'Drops by stage'.
findings.scenario: A collapsed strip shows '3 dropped' and the user can't tell whether the recording or the Zoom output lost frames.
findings.recommendation: Name them: 'Recording · 3 frames dropped' vs 'Output · 3 drops'; collapsed warning states which.

findings.issue: 'Output' names three concepts: the picture-signal choice (Output vs Source pop-up on each picture), the strip's virtual-camera row, and the sidebar/status bar destination.
findings.evidence: tile() bottom-left `${f.signal}` = 'Output'; strip output row 'Ultracam · Feed 1'; sidebar 'Output' section.
findings.scenario: 'Output' on the picture is read as 'what's going out', which is true only when processing is on and the feed is published.
findings.recommendation: Picture pop-up: 'Processed / Source' (or 'As sent / Camera'). Keep 'Output' for the destination only.

findings.location: placement of rare vs session decisions
findings.issue: Set-once automation switches occupy permanent sidebar space, while Output mode, a per-session decision that locks once live, appears only in Settings, the Program menu and the dropdown.
findings.evidence: r3.js sidebar() Automation section; settings.html Camera 'Output mode · Change while stopped'; sidebar Output section has no mode control.
findings.scenario: Before a two-camera meeting the user must go to Settings to switch to Program mode.
findings.recommendation: Sidebar Output header gets a Separate/Program segmented control (enabled while stopped, locked note while live). Automation moves to Settings + ⋯ with a one-line sidebar summary.

findings.issue: Video preview appears as a Settings toggle, a dropdown row (⇧⌘P) and a tile 'Hide Preview' context item; it is per-feed runtime state in code, so its scope and home are unclear.
findings.evidence: settings.html General 'Video preview'; FeedDescriptor.previewEnabled; AppModel.previewEnabled (selected feed); monitor-tools context menu 'Hide Preview'.
findings.scenario: User hides preview in Settings and can't find why one picture is black.
findings.recommendation: Runtime only: View menu + picture context menu, scoped and named per feed ('Hide Feed 2 Preview'); remove from Settings.

findings.issue: Add Camera (+) and Rename… look available while feeds run or record, but the model blocks add/remove/rename until all sources stop and no take is active.
findings.evidence: AppModel.canEditFeedTopology false when any source active or recording; r3.js sidebar '+' always enabled; main-collapsed popover Rename… enabled (only Remove shows 'Stop Feed 2 to remove it').
findings.scenario: User tries to rename a camera mid-recording; nothing happens.
findings.recommendation: Show them disabled with the reason ('Stop all feeds to add a camera'), or make rename live-safe in the model.

findings.issue: A drive-level 'time left' (which depends on how many feeds write to that drive) is printed in each strip as if it were that feed's own budget.
findings.evidence: Feed 1 strip '8TB › Takes › Feed 1 · 1 h 35 m left' equals sidebar '8TB 1 h 35 m left' for 2 takes.
findings.scenario: User stops Feed 2 and expects Feed 1's figure to stay the same; it doubles.
findings.recommendation: Strip: '8TB · 1 h 35 m left with 2 takes'; drive figure lives in sidebar/status bar.

findings.location: Whole channel column + toolbar + sidebar (red usage)
findings.issue: Red is used for about 11 different marks on one screen, so the operator can't tell on air from recording from stop from error at a glance.
findings.evidence: main-expanded Feed 1 column alone has: the picture tally ring, the 'ON AIR · Program' badge, the REC dot pill, the strip's red 'RECORDING' label, the red stop-square record button, and the 'On air in Program' badge. The toolbar adds a red Feed 1 cut pill and a red '■ 12:31 · 2' button. The sidebar has a red camera dot, the red backup dot and the red max marker on the shot timer. The status bar has a REC dot. Crops: /tmp/l4/me-pic1.png, me-strip1.png, me-toolbar.png.
findings.scenario: Mid-meeting, the user glances at the window to check what Zoom is getting. Both columns show red (Feed 2 has REC and a red record button too), so 'which one is live' takes reading rather than glancing.
findings.recommendation: Give each meaning its own shape. Solid red fill and the ring are reserved for ON AIR, meaning what a consumer receives. Recording becomes a small red dot plus neutral text ('REC 12:31' in primary label color, no red 'RECORDING' caption). The record control is a neutral ring with a red dot that becomes a neutral square while recording. Errors use orange or red with an exclamation icon, never plain red text. The shot timer's max marker turns neutral.
alternatives: Keep red for REC and use a broadcast-style amber/red 'PGM' lamp for on air
Recording as a pulsing dot with no other red

findings.location: Picture overlays, top row (524 pt picture)
findings.issue: All four picture corners are permanently filled. On a 524 pt picture the top row (key badge, feed pill, role badge, five-button tool group) leaves about 25 pt free and covers the top of the image. This is the clutter the user asked to reduce.
findings.evidence: Crop /tmp/l4/me-pic1.png: '1' key, 'Feed 1 ⌃', 'ON AIR · Program' and the five tool buttons span the full width. The bottom row is filled too: TC, 'Output ⌃', REC. The r3.js tile() always renders the tool group unless compact.
findings.scenario: During a meeting the user wants to see framing and headroom. The overlays sit right where the talent's head is in a tight shot.
findings.recommendation: At rest show only the identity (feed name with role badge merged, e.g. a red-tinted 'Feed 1 · ON AIR' pill) and REC. Tools, the Output/Source picker, freeze, clean, zoom and detach appear on hover or keyboard focus. The timecode moves into the strip, or appears on hover. Drop the separate '1' key badge; the number can live in the pill ('1 Feed 1') or in the toolbar cut buttons only.
alternatives: One overflow '⋯' glass button at the top right that reveals the tool group
Tool state as a single summary chip ('Zebra · Guides') at rest, full group on hover

findings.issue: The pages disagree on whether the picture tool group is visible at rest. main-expanded and standalone always show it; four-up and monitor-tools show it only on hover.
findings.evidence: four-up legend 5: 'At rest only the name, state, timecode and REC stay visible.' The main-expanded crop shows the tools at rest on both pictures.
findings.scenario: An engineer can't tell which behavior to build, and the user reviewing mockups judges clutter from the busier version.
findings.recommendation: Make hover/focus reveal the rule everywhere (see L4-02), and re-render main-expanded, main-collapsed, standalone, single and program-view.
alternatives: Show it at rest only on the focused tile

findings.issue: Cutting to a feed can be done from four places in the window, all drawn at once: toolbar cut pills, clicking the picture, the strip 'Cut to Feed 2 ⌃2' button, and the ⌃1/⌃2 hints in the sidebar. Each repeats the same red/green state.
findings.evidence: main-expanded toolbar ('1 Feed 1' red, '2 Feed 2' green outline), picture tally rings, the strip Output row ('On air in Program' badge, 'Cut to Feed 2' button), sidebar camera rows with ⌃1/⌃2. Crop /tmp/l4/me-strip-row.png.
findings.scenario: The tally state is drawn three to four times. That adds noise, and it makes the meaning of clicking each element less obvious (see S1).
findings.recommendation: Keep one primary cut surface: the toolbar cut buttons, or a cut bar, plus ⌃n. Tally lives on the pictures only. Remove the strip's 'Cut to' button and the 'On air in Program' badge, since the picture ring already says so. Sidebar rows keep only a small tally dot.
alternatives: Keep the strip button and drop the toolbar pills (less central, scales worse to 4 feeds)

findings.issue: One recording is shown up to seven times at the same weight, so the more important 'what is live' signal gets drowned out.
findings.evidence: main-expanded: sidebar camera rows ('REC 12:31' ×2), the sidebar Recording section, picture REC pills ×2, strip elapsed ×2, the toolbar '12:31 · 2', the status bar 'REC 2 feeds 12:31', the menu bar icon dot.
findings.scenario: The user scans for problems. With 'REC 12:31' repeated everywhere, a single orange 'Paused' or 'dropped' is easy to miss.
findings.recommendation: Define one primary place (the strip: elapsed, size, drops) and quiet echoes (a small REC dot on the picture, the status bar summary, the menu bar dot). Remove 'REC 12:31' from the sidebar camera rows and drop the duplicate elapsed time in the toolbar button (show 'Stop All' with a count).
alternatives: Make the status bar the single summary and remove the sidebar Recording section

findings.issue: The most prominent control in the window (filled red capsule) is labelled only with a stop glyph, a time and a bare number. It doesn't say what it does.
findings.evidence: Crop /tmp/l4/me-toolbar.png: the red '■ 12:31 · 2' at the far right. On standalone the same slot says 'Stop All · 12:31', so the label varies by page.
findings.scenario: After the meeting the user wants to stop the backup. It's unclear whether this stops recording, the feeds or the meeting.
findings.recommendation: Label it with its action: 'Record All' when idle, and 'Stop All (2)' plus elapsed time in a quieter secondary style when recording. Consider making it non-filled while recording so the red fill stays exclusive to on air (L4-01).
alternatives: Split it into a 'REC 12:31 · 2' status chip and a separate Stop All button

findings.location: Collapsed strip hover: Stop button next to the stop-square record button
findings.issue: In the collapsed strip's hover state, a 'Stop' button sits right next to the record control, which is already showing a stop square. That's two stop affordances 100 pt apart, plus Pause.
findings.evidence: Crop /tmp/l4/mc-strips.png: Feed 1 row shows '‖ Pause', '■ Stop', a meter, then the red ■-in-ring record button and ⋯.
findings.scenario: The user wants to pause and hits the wrong one. A stopped take can't be undone.
findings.recommendation: The record control is the single record/stop toggle. Pause is a separate secondary icon button. The hover state adds nothing else. The text 'Stop' button is dropped from collapsed rows, or replaces the toggle, not both.
alternatives: Expanded strips only expose Pause/Stop; collapsed shows just the toggle

findings.location: Strip Output row: effect chips + unlabeled switch
findings.issue: The Output row ends with four effect chips and an unlabeled green switch. It's not clear whether the chips are toggles or status, or that the switch is Processing (complete bypass). The most consequential control in the row has no label.
findings.evidence:
Crop /tmp/l4/me-strip-row.png: 'LUT 1080p 4:2:0 29.97' then a bare switch. r3.js strip() renders `
` with no text.
findings.scenario: The user flips the switch to 'turn LUT off' and instead bypasses everything, including the downscale. That changes the output format mid-meeting (S3).
findings.recommendation: Label it ('Processing'), or replace the chips + switch with one 'Effects' pop-up button showing a summary ('LUT · 1080p · 4:2:0') that opens the ordered checklist. Bypass gets a distinct, labelled control. Chips, if kept, need a pressed/unpressed button style distinct from status badges.
alternatives: Chips as status only; edits only via ⋯ popover

findings.issue: Every expanded strip repeats constant information that is the same for all feeds and never changes during a session ('ProRes 422 · clean source', the full camera/device name, 'Live · 2160p 59.94'). That's about 20% of strip text with no operational value.
findings.evidence: Crop /tmp/l4/me-strip1.png: header 'FX3 · Mini Recorder 12G' plus the 'Live · 2160p 59.94' badge, and the folder row's 'ProRes 422 · clean source'. The same appears in Feed 2's strip.
findings.scenario: The strip reads as a dense form instead of a status line, which pushes the user toward collapsing it and losing the useful parts.
findings.recommendation: Show codec/'clean source' once (sidebar Recording section or Settings), and per strip only when it differs. Move the device name to a tooltip or the ⋯ popover. Show the format badge only when it's unusual (e.g. 29.97 vs 59.94 mismatch) or on hover.
alternatives: Keep the device name but drop the format badge (the sidebar already shows it)

findings.issue: Collapsing strips doesn't make the screen calmer. The freed space is immediately filled with two scopes and a director timeline, so the collapsed page has as much ink as the expanded one. With the sidebar visible the pictures are width-limited (524 pt) and can't grow.
findings.evidence: main-collapsed.png: the strips become one line, then a 138 pt scope per feed and a full-width timeline with lanes, speech bars and cut rows. Picture size is identical to main-expanded.
findings.scenario: The user collapses strips to reduce clutter during a meeting and sees no reduction.
findings.recommendation: Define collapse as a calm meeting state. Scopes and the timeline are off by default and are added explicitly (⌥⌘K, View menu). Empty space stays empty, or the pictures grow. Offer 'Focus' (⌃⌘S hides the sidebar) so two pictures grow to about 646 pt. Show this calm state as a mockup.
alternatives: Stacked layout (pictures one above the other) when the window is tall and narrow

findings.issue: With 1–2 cameras the sidebar's camera rows repeat what the strips and pictures show (name, format, REC). The lower third of the sidebar is empty (about 200 pt below Automation on main-expanded), so the sidebar costs 244 pt of picture width for little unique information.
findings.evidence: Crop /tmp/l4/me-sb.png: Cameras rows 'Feed 1 · 2160p 59.94 · REC 12:31'. The full main-expanded.png shows the empty sidebar below the Automation section.
findings.scenario: Two-camera meeting: pictures are 524 pt wide instead of about 646 pt because of a panel whose top section duplicates the strips.
findings.recommendation: Drop or shrink the Cameras section when every camera already has a channel (keep only '+ Add Camera' in the section header). Lead with unique session content (Output/Program, Recording destination, Recent takes, Automation). Consider a narrower sidebar (200–210 pt), and remember the hidden state per layout.
alternatives: Collapse the sidebar to a 64 pt rail by default with 2+ cameras

findings.issue: The collapse-all-strips toggle uses a sliders icon, which reads as 'settings/adjustments'. It sits between the layout picker and Record with no label.
findings.evidence: Crop /tmp/l4/me-toolbar.png: the lone sliders glyph capsule. r3.js toolbar() uses ic('sliders').
findings.scenario: The user looks for display settings, clicks it and the strips vanish. Or they never find the collapse function the legend describes.
findings.recommendation: Use a symbol that means 'compact rows' (e.g. a rectangle.compress.vertical-style glyph) with a 'Compact' label or tooltip, or move it into the View menu only (⌥⌘S) and drop it from the toolbar.
alternatives: Segmented 'Detailed | Compact' control next to the layout picker

findings.location: Program picture + Feed 1 tile both ringed red
findings.issue: In Program view the same image is shown twice with the same red ring: the large Program picture and the Feed 1 source tile. That's double red emphasis on identical content, and it weakens the 'which source is on air' cue.
findings.evidence: program-view.png: the Program picture has a red ring plus 'ON AIR · Zoom'; Feed 1 has a red ring plus 'ON AIR · Program'.
findings.scenario: The eye bounces between two red frames showing the same face.
findings.recommendation: The Program picture gets a neutral frame with a 'PGM → Zoom' label (it is the output, not a source). Tally rings are for sources only.
alternatives: Thin red top bar on Program instead of a full ring

findings.issue: The dropdown is about 700 pt tall with 18–22 rows plus preview. It fits a 13" MacBook Air (about 919 pt usable) with two feeds, but leaves little margin once a banner is added (menubar g) or with 3–4 cameras. Several rows duplicate each other (Stop Feed vs Stop Recording, separate Effects/LUT/Capture Input rows, two automation rows).
findings.evidence: Crop /tmp/l4/single-dd.png: preview plus 17 rows plus the stat line, about 690 pt. In menubar.png, variant (a) has 2 thumbnails plus 14 rows plus the Feed 1 submenu; variant (g) adds two banners.
findings.scenario: Laptop user with 4 cameras and an attention banner: the menu reaches the Dock or scrolls, which NSMenu does with arrows.
findings.recommendation: Fold per-feed rows into one 'Feed 1 ›' submenu per camera (Effects, LUT, Input, Recording). Merge the automation toggles under 'Automation ›'. Cap the top level at about 12 rows, and keep the preview height fixed at about 180 pt.
alternatives: Preview collapsible with a disclosure row
Show the stat line only on ⌥-click

findings.issue: Purple NEW tags appear inline in the UI (sidebar, status bar, dropdown rows, settings rows), often several per screen. They add a fourth accent color and distort the clutter judgement the user is making. Some sit mid-label and wrap ('Record with camera apps' then a NEW tag on its own line).
findings.evidence: Crop /tmp/l4/me-sb.png: NEW after '8TB', after 'Recent Takes', and on a second line under 'Record with camera apps'. Crop me-sbar.png: NEW in the status bar. single-dd.png: two NEW tags in menu rows.
findings.scenario: The user evaluates density with annotation chrome that won't ship, and approves or rejects layouts for the wrong reason.
findings.recommendation: Render a 'production' variant of each key page with NEW tags hidden (a CSS toggle such as body.clean .newtag{display:none}). Mark proposals only in the legend, or with a subtle dotted underline.
alternatives: Keep tags but render them outside the UI as margin callouts

findings.location: Right column: two scopes always on
findings.issue: The everyday one-camera meeting page dedicates a 252 pt column to two stacked scopes (luma plus parade) at rest. That makes the most common, simplest use case look like the busiest technical page.
findings.evidence: single.png: the right column holds Luma Waveform and RGB Parade, full height. The signal path card adds a third information block under the strip.
findings.scenario: A meeting user who never reads scopes sees a control room, which is the opposite of the 'just works in Zoom' path.
findings.recommendation: Default single-camera meetings to the picture only (larger, about 1060 pt wide) with the strip below. Scopes and the signal path appear when toggled. Show that default as the hero for the one-camera case.
alternatives: One scope only, matching the picture tool toggle

findings.issue: A lot of status rides on 10–10.5 pt tertiary-gray text (sidebar sublines, strip folder and time-left, collapsed sizes, status bar), which is hard to read at arm's length on a second display during a call.
findings.evidence: Crop /tmp/l4/me-sb.png: '12:31 · 27.5 GB · ProRes 422' and 'Feed 1_2026-10-20_08-...' at about 10 pt mid-gray. me-strip1.png: '1 h 35 m left' and 'ProRes 422 · clean source' in --label2/--label3.
findings.scenario: The user checks time left on the drive from across the desk and can't read it.
findings.recommendation: Minimum 11 pt for status values, and use secondary (not tertiary) color for anything operational (time left, drops, size). Reserve tertiary for truly decorative captions. L6 should measure contrast.

findings.location: Side margins and the no-signal tile
findings.issue: Four Up uses fixed 574 pt columns, leaving about 70 pt black margins at each side. The No signal tile is a large pure-black block with centered text, the highest-contrast element on the page, so an inactive camera draws the most attention.
findings.evidence: four-up.png: empty gutters left of Feed 1/3 and right of Feed 2/4. Feed 3 is a black tile with 'No HDMI signal'.
findings.scenario: The operator's eye lands on the dead camera instead of the on-air one.
findings.recommendation: No-signal tiles use the window's content fill (not black) with muted text and a smaller icon. Center the grid with symmetric gaps, or let tiles fill the width and letterbox inside each tile.
alternatives: Collapse a no-signal tile to a compact card and give its space to the others

findings.issue: Verdict: CONFIRMED. See L4-01.
findings.evidence: About 11 red marks on main-expanded across sidebar, toolbar, pictures, strips and status bar.
findings.recommendation: See L4-01.

findings.issue: Verdict: CONFIRMED, and the actual count is up to seven. See L4-05.
findings.evidence: Sidebar rows, the sidebar Recording section, picture pills, strip elapsed, toolbar, status bar, menu bar icon.
findings.recommendation: See L4-05.

findings.issue: Verdict: CONFIRMED visually. The toolbar's red '■ 12:31 · 2', the strip 'Stop', the stop-square record button and the toolbar 'Stop' (feed) all use the same ■ glyph for different scopes. See L4-06 and L4-07.
findings.evidence: Crops me-toolbar.png and mc-strips.png.
findings.recommendation: Each stop names its scope ('Stop Recording', 'Stop Feed', 'Stop All (2)'), and ■ is used only on the record toggle.

findings.issue: Verdict: CONFIRMED, plus an inconsistency: Four Up already hides tools at rest. See L4-02 and L4-03.
findings.evidence: Crop me-pic1.png: about 25 pt free in the top row.
findings.recommendation: Show tools on hover/focus only, everywhere.

findings.issue: Verdict: CONFIRMED for 1–2 cameras. In Four Up the sidebar is hidden, so it doesn't apply there. See L4-11.
findings.evidence: Crop me-sb.png.
findings.recommendation: See L4-11.

findings.issue: Verdict: PARTLY CONFIRMED. About 700 pt fits a 13" Air with two feeds, but there's little headroom with banners or 3–4 cameras. See L4-14.
findings.evidence: Crop single-dd.png, about 690 pt.
findings.recommendation: See L4-14.

findings.issue: Verdict: CONFIRMED visually (L7 owns the details). A paused feed gets an orange ring on standalone but no ring on four-up. Collapsed rows show effect chips on four-up/program-view, but hand-built hover rows on main-collapsed drop them.
findings.evidence: standalone.png Feed 2 (orange ring) vs four-up.png Feed 4 (no ring). main-collapsed Feed 1 hover row without chips.
findings.recommendation: Add paused, no-signal and hover states to the r3.js builders and re-render.

findings.location: Single click on a feed picture
findings.issue: Single click on a picture cuts Program to it, breaking the macOS convention that a single click selects/focuses and an action needs an explicit control or a double-click. The same click also focuses the tile.
findings.evidence: main-expanded legend 2: 'Click a picture or press ⌃1/⌃2 to cut'; monitor-tools keyboard card: 'Click a tile to focus it (blue ring)'; MonitorWorkspaceShell.swift surface(): .simultaneousGesture(TapGesture().onEnded { focusedTile = index }).
findings.scenario: Mid-meeting the user clicks Feed 2 to adjust its zebra; Zoom cuts to Feed 2.
findings.recommendation: Single click selects and focuses the feed. Make that the visible selected-feed state, which also resolves S2. Cut only from explicit controls: toolbar cut group, the strip's 'Cut to Feed N', ⌃1–⌃4 and the Program menu.
alternatives: Double-click to cut (HIG default-action pattern, still risky live)
⌥-click to cut
Cut only from the cut bar in Program view
affects: menubar (thumbnails as cut buttons are acceptable: menus are explicit)

findings.issue: The ⋯ popover is about 850 pt tall with six grouped sections, a file picker and a destructive Remove Camera. HIG reserves popovers for a small amount of transient content. A popover this size covers the pictures it configures and dismisses on any outside click.
findings.evidence: main-collapsed: popover spans y≈80–950 of the 1170 desktop; sections Source, Processing, LUT, Recording, Output, Monitor; footer Rename…, Diagnostics…, Remove Camera.
findings.scenario: The user opens ⋯ to load a LUT, the NSOpenPanel takes focus and the popover dismisses, losing context. Or they can't see the picture while toggling effects.
findings.recommendation: Turn ⋯ into a Menu: Rename…, Load LUT…, Copy Monitor Settings To ›, Show Diagnostics, separator, Remove Camera… (role .destructive + confirmationDialog). Put the full per-feed form in an on-demand .inspector (macOS 14+) that's closed by default. This respects 'no inspector' as the resting state, keeps the pictures visible and survives file panels.
alternatives: A sheet per feed (modal, blocks monitoring)
Split into two small popovers: Processing+LUT, and Source+Recording

findings.location: Picture tool buttons: settings via long-press / ⌥-click
findings.issue: Tool settings open through long-press or ⌥-click on a toggle button. Neither is a macOS button convention, so the settings are undiscoverable. 'Hold Clean' press-and-hold has the same problem.
findings.evidence: monitor-tools section header: 'click again or open its popover (long-press / ⌥-click) for settings'. Hold Clean in the overlay anatomy.
findings.scenario: The user wants to change the zebra threshold and can't find how; the button only toggles.
findings.recommendation: Use the native split pull-down: Menu(content:label:primaryAction:) (verified, macOS 12+). Clicking the face toggles the tool and the attached chevron opens its settings. Also put tool settings in the tile context menu and in View ▸ Monitor Tools ›. Keep Hold Clean as a keyboard hold (⌃⌥C held) with the toggle as the visible control.
alternatives: A single 'Tools' pull-down per picture listing all five with toggles and 'Settings…'
Right-click only (still hidden)

findings.issue: The dropdown needs live video plus native menu rows. MenuBarExtra(.menu) can't host video, and .window (WindowMenuBarExtraStyle) loses real menu behavior. The recommended NSStatusItem + NSMenu + NSMenuItem.view is real AppKit API, but custom-view items get no keyboard highlight and don't auto-dismiss on click. The live layer also has to render during menu event tracking. Clickable cut thumbnails inside a view item are fully custom.
findings.evidence: SDK: NSMenuItem.view (macos 10.5), subtitle (macos 14.4; shown on 15+), sectionHeaderWithTitle (14.0), badge (14.0) in NSMenuItem.h; WindowMenuBarExtraStyle in SwiftUI interface. menubar (a): 'thumbnails act as cut buttons'.
findings.scenario: Implementation finds the preview frozen while the menu tracks, or arrow keys skip the cut thumbnails, so cuts can't be done from the keyboard.
findings.recommendation: Spike first. Build rows natively: NSMenuItem.subtitle for 'Recording 12:31' (not inline gray text), sectionHeader for 'Cameras'/'Recording', badge for counts. Make cut targets regular NSMenuItems ('Cut to Feed 2 ⌃2') whose image is a still thumbnail refreshed at about 1 Hz, rather than live clickable views. Keep exactly one custom view: the preview.
alternatives: MenuBarExtra(.window) with hand-built menu-styled rows (easy video, custom keyboard nav and submenus)

findings.issue: The Program and single-camera dropdowns are about 700–770 pt tall (preview 178, thumbnails ~110, ~21 rows × 25). On a 13" MacBook Air at the 'Larger Text' display setting (1024×640 pt), or on small external displays, NSMenu shows scroll arrows and the top custom preview item scrolls away.
findings.evidence: menubar.png (a) spans y≈95–770 and (b) y≈95–785 at 1× points; the rows include separate Open Ultracam / Settings… / Quit plus a stat line.
findings.scenario: A laptop user at larger text opens the menu and has to scroll to reach Stop Recording.
findings.recommendation: Cap at about 12 top-level rows. Fold Effects/LUT/Input into the Feed N › submenu, put Pause and Show in Finder under Recording ›, and merge Open/Settings into the footer. Shrink the preview to 300×169 and drop the separate stat line (it's in the status bar and diagnostics).
alternatives: Collapse the preview to a 1-line status row when screen height < 800 pt

findings.issue: The proposed red recording dot and orange attention dot break the template-image convention for status items and collide with the system privacy indicators (orange = microphone in use, green = camera in use).
findings.evidence: menubar icon states: 'Recording red dot NEW', 'Attention orange dot NEW'; settings General 'Show attention dot for problems'.
findings.scenario: The user sees an orange dot near the clock and thinks their microphone is live, or misses that the dot belongs to Ultracam.
findings.recommendation: Keep the status item a template image. Show state through symbol variants (e.g. video.fill / arrow.right.square / a 'record' glyph badge / exclamationmark.triangle). If color is kept, use red for recording only and never orange.
alternatives: Monochrome badge dot (template) plus the accessibility label carrying the state

findings.location: Status bar spanning beneath the floating sidebar
findings.issue: The mockups draw a window-wide status bar with the floating glass sidebar ending above it. NavigationSplitView's macOS 26+ floating sidebar runs the full window height. A window-wide bottom bar under it isn't the native layout, and .safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom) on the split view may not produce it.
findings.evidence: spec §1: 'Sidebar … ends 8 above status bar'; spec §4 status bar = .safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom). Every main-window mockup shows the sidebar stopping at the bar.
findings.scenario: Engineering builds it natively and the bar ends up only under the detail column or overlapping the sidebar, so the design doesn't match.
findings.recommendation: Design the status bar in the detail column only (the sidebar keeps full height), applied to the detail view. Update measurements in spec §1. Verify in the window spike.
alternatives: A custom container instead of NavigationSplitView (loses native sidebar behavior)

findings.issue: The toolbar carries title + cut group (3) + layout picker (4) + collapse toggle + record. At the specified 980 pt minimum it overflows into the » menu, which can hide live cut buttons. The record item shows only '12:31 · 2' with no verb. The collapse toggle uses a 'sliders' (adjust/filter) symbol with only a title attribute.
findings.evidence: r3.js toolbar(): tb-btn title='Collapse strips' with ic('sliders'); prominent record shows `${recLabel}` only. spec §1 minimum 980×680.
findings.scenario: At a small window size Feed 2's cut button goes into the overflow menu mid-meeting. The user can't tell whether the red '12:31 · 2' button stops everything.
findings.recommendation: Give every ToolbarItem a Label (text + symbol) so Icon+Text mode and customization work. Set ToolbarItemVisibilityPriority (macOS 26, verified) high for cuts and record, low for layout and collapse. Label the record item 'Stop All' / 'Record All' with elapsed as secondary. Use a collapse symbol such as rectangle.compress.vertical.
alternatives: Move the layout picker into View menu / toolbar title menu (toolbarTitleMenu, macOS 13)

findings.issue: Glass controls stay on the video permanently: identity, role, five tool buttons, timecode, signal picker, REC. Liquid Glass treats glass as a floating controls layer. Video players (AVKit/QuickTime) auto-hide chrome over content. Always-on glass over bright regions also loses legibility.
findings.evidence: main-expanded: tool group top-right and TC/Output bottom-left on both pictures at rest. Only Four Up hides the tool group until hover.
findings.scenario: Pills over the bright window region in the frame are hard to read, and they block framing checks.
findings.recommendation: At rest show only identity + tally badge + REC. Reveal the tools, signal picker and TC on hover or keyboard focus (as Four Up already does). Group the pills in a GlassEffectContainer and use the opaque material under Reduce Transparency.
alternatives: Move the tool toggles into the strip header
Keep TC permanently only when Timecode is enabled in a View setting

findings.issue: The sidebar is built as a NavigationSplitView source list but works as a control panel. Camera rows aren't selectable; it holds switches, a strategy pop-up, a shot timer and a Recover button. Sidebars in macOS denote navigation and selection, and VoiceOver announces them that way.
findings.evidence: r3.js sidebar(): camera rows with no selection binding (first row has a static highlight); Auto switching switch, strategy popup, automation switches.
findings.scenario: The user clicks Feed 2 in the sidebar expecting it to become the target of ⇧⌘B/Feed menu; nothing happens.
findings.recommendation: Bind the Cameras List selection to selectedFeedID, which gives a visible selected feed (S2) and native keyboard selection. Keep Output/Recording/Takes as rows that open popovers or reveal in Finder. Move the set-once automation switches to the Feed/Record menus + Settings, leaving status in the sidebar.
alternatives: Keep it as a non-navigational leading panel (custom HStack) instead of NavigationSplitView

findings.issue: ⌘0 is proposed twice: Window ▸ Ultracam (main window) in app-menus/spec, and 'Fit ⌘0' picture zoom in monitor-tools. ⌘= / ⌘− zoom appear only in monitor-tools: they're missing from the app-menus View menu and spec §6, and aren't marked NEW.
findings.evidence: app-menus.html row('Ultracam', key '⌘0'); spec.html row ⌘0 Main window; monitor-tools.html keyrow '⌘ = ⌘ − Zoom in / out, ⌘0 to fit' and pill 'Fit ⌘0'.
findings.scenario: The engineer implements both and one shortcut silently wins.
findings.recommendation: Use View ▸ Zoom In ⌘= / Zoom Out ⌘− / Zoom to Fit ⌥⌘0 (or ⌘9), keep ⌘0 for the main window, and add them to app-menus and the spec table with the NEW tag.
alternatives: Drop ⌘0 for the main window (Window menu item without a shortcut)

findings.issue: Quitting while recording is drawn as a sheet on the main window. In menu-bar-only mode (Hide from Dock, window closed), which is the common meeting setup, there's no window to attach a sheet to.
findings.evidence: states §6 'Quit while recording' sheet over a window; UltracamApp.swift applicationShouldTerminate returns .terminateLater while recordings finish.
findings.scenario: The user quits from the menu bar with the window closed; nothing visible explains why the app hasn't quit.
findings.recommendation: Use an app-modal NSAlert (or a small standalone 'Finishing recordings' panel) when no main window is visible; use a sheet only when the window is open.
alternatives: Open the main window, then show the sheet

findings.issue: Settings duplicates live view state that belongs in the View menu: Session sidebar Show/Hide (⌃⌘S) and Video preview (⇧⌘P). HIG keeps Settings for preferences, not toggles that change the current window.
findings.evidence: settings General: 'Session sidebar  Show', 'Video preview' switch with ⇧⌘P.
findings.scenario: The user toggles the preview in Settings and in the View menu, and can't tell which is authoritative.
findings.recommendation: Remove both from Settings, or rephrase as launch defaults ('Show sidebar when the window opens').

findings.issue: The destructive Remove Camera sits in a row next to Rename… and Diagnostics…, with no separation or confirmation. 'Diagnostics…' uses an ellipsis though it opens a window without asking for more input.
findings.evidence: main-collapsed.html: Rename…Diagnostics… + red Remove Camera.
findings.scenario: The user misclicks Remove Camera next to Diagnostics once the feed is stopped.
findings.recommendation: Put destructive actions after a separator in a Menu with role .destructive and a confirmationDialog. Rename the window command 'Show Diagnostics' (no ellipsis).

findings.issue: TabsPickerStyle / .pickerStyle(.tabs) is verified in MacOSX27.0.sdk (macOS 27.0), but its appearance is unverified. The mockups draw a segmented capsule, and the real control may render as a toolbar tab bar.
findings.evidence: SDK: 'public struct TabsPickerStyle : SwiftUI.PickerStyle' @available(macOS 27.0); diagnostics.html tab control drawn as a segmented capsule.
findings.scenario: The built Diagnostics window doesn't match the mockup, and its tabs land somewhere unexpected.
findings.recommendation: Render .tabs in a scratch build before finalizing. Fall back to Picker(.segmented) in the principal toolbar item, the established pattern for switching a window among 2–4 peers.

findings.issue: Effect chips (LUT/1080p/4:2:0/29.97) look like passive tags, not toggles. The round record button is custom-drawn. Neither is a native control as drawn, so toggle affordance, accessibility traits and keyboard activation have to be rebuilt.
findings.evidence: r3.js fxChips() spans; .recbtn CSS circle; spec §4 maps chips to Toggle(.button).
findings.scenario: The user doesn't realize tapping '4:2:0' changes what Zoom receives, or does it by accident thinking it's a label.
findings.recommendation: Use Toggle with .toggleStyle(.button) inside a ControlGroup (bordered when on, with a help tag), and a Button with record.circle / stop.circle.fill symbols, tinted red with a glassProminent or bordered style. Native controls bring keyboard and VoiceOver support for free.
alternatives: Make chips read-only status and edit effects only in the Feed menu/inspector

findings.issue: WindowGroup(for: MonitorTargetID.self) is buildable: the API is verified (macOS 13+) and MonitorTargetID is Hashable + Codable. But WindowGroup windows restore at relaunch by default, which would reopen monitor surfaces and start GPU work at launch.
findings.evidence: SDK WindowGroup init<D,C>(id:for:) ; MonitorConfiguration.swift: struct MonitorTargetID: RawRepresentable, Hashable, Codable; restorationBehavior(_:) available macOS 15.
findings.scenario: Ultracam launches in the menu bar and silently reopens two monitor windows from last session.
findings.recommendation: Apply .restorationBehavior(.disabled) to the monitor WindowGroup (or decide restoration deliberately), and note it in spec §4/§9.

findings.location: picture overlay pills (feed name, Output/Source picker, timecode, REC) over bright picture areas
findings.issue: Overlay text on glass pills loses contrast over bright video: primary label 3.21:1 and secondary 1.98:1 over a bright window region. Both are below the WCAG 4.5:1 minimum for 11–12 pt text. The 52% glass has no guaranteed backing.
findings.evidence: kit.css .glass rgba(44,44,48,0.52) + --label 0.88 / --label2 0.56; computed over #dfe9ee (the scene's window) = 3.21 and 1.98; over mid-tone wall = 7.40. The Feed 1 pill sits on the bright window in main-expanded/single.
findings.scenario: A presenter by a bright window or a white wall can't read 'REC 12:31' or the Output/Source label on the picture they're watching.
findings.recommendation: Give picture overlays a guaranteed scrim: a darker capsule (≈ 75% black under the glass) or a top/bottom gradient scrim, and keep primary-weight text only. Spec says overlays stay dark in Light mode; add a minimum-contrast rule (≥ 4.5:1 against white video).
alternatives: Edge gradient scrim (top 56 pt, bottom 44 pt) behind all overlays
Move timecode and REC into the strip and keep only the identity chip on the picture

findings.issue: The sidebar camera rows show on air vs next only as a red or green dot, with no text. Red vs green differ by luminance ratio 1.68, so they're indistinguishable with protan/deutan color blindness. The pictures carry text badges; the sidebar doesn't.
findings.evidence: r3.js sidebar(): tally = '<span class="dot red">' / '<span class="dot green">'; row text is only '2160p 59.94 · REC 12:31'. Computed red #ff453a vs green #30d158 = 1.68:1.
findings.scenario: A red-green colorblind operator uses the sidebar to check which camera is in Program and reads both rows as the same.
findings.recommendation: Add the role word to the row subtitle ('On air', 'Next') or a shaped glyph (filled dot vs ring), matching the strip badges. VoiceOver label: 'Feed 1, on air in Program, recording'.
alternatives: Use the same text badge component as the collapsed strip
Show a small 'ON AIR' pill on the row and drop the dot

findings.issue: Effect chips show on vs off only by tint: blue-tinted with light-blue text vs grey with tertiary text. Off-chip text is 2.46:1 and there's no shape, icon or text difference. Collapsed chips are 9.5 pt.
findings.evidence: r2.css .fx span / .fx span.on; r3.js fxChips(small) font-size 9.5px; computed label3 on fill2 = 2.46. Only bypass adds strikethrough.
findings.scenario: In a meeting, an operator with low vision or color deficiency can't tell whether the LUT chip is on, so they don't know what Zoom is getting.
findings.recommendation: Encode state with shape: filled chip plus a checkmark for on, outlined or hollow for off. Raise off-chip text to secondary (≥ 4.5:1) and minimum 10 pt. Give each chip a VoiceOver label: 'LUT on'.
alternatives: Show only enabled effects as chips ('LUT · 1080p · 4:2:0') as plain text
Toggle-style capsules (native Toggle .button) whose on state is shown by fill and checkmark

findings.location: tertiary text (.c3, .k2 labels, '—' values, shortcut hints, 'ProRes 422 · clean source', 'Not published')
findings.issue: Tertiary label color measures 2.5–2.65:1 on every surface (window, card fill, sidebar glass, dropdown), yet it carries real information: section labels (AUDIO, RECORDING), shortcut hints (⌃2), codec/source note, 'Not published', 'Not in use'. That fails WCAG 1.4.3 for informational text. Light mode is worse (secondary 3.5:1, tertiary 1.85:1).
findings.evidence: Computed: label3 on window 2.65, on fill 2.56, on sidebar 2.53, on dropdown 2.57; light label2 3.50, label3 1.85. r3.js: 'ProRes 422 · clean source', cut-button '⌃n' hint in c3; .k2 uses --label3 (r2.css).
findings.scenario: A user with mild low vision can't read 'Not published' or the recording format; in Light mode secondary values like time left and file size become hard to read.
findings.recommendation: Reserve tertiary for decoration and disabled state. Informational values (time left, size, codec, published state, section labels) use secondary or primary. Rely on the system's Increase Contrast and test both appearances. Spec §2 should state 'no essential information in tertiary'.
alternatives: Promote section labels to secondary semibold caption
Drop low-value tertiary text entirely (e.g. 'ProRes 422 · clean source' can live in the ⋯ popover)

findings.location: small badges and role pills ('On air in Program', 'ON AIR', 'Next', default badges)
findings.issue: Several status badges miss 4.5:1 at their size: red badge text on tinted red 3.97:1, white on the 92% red role pill 3.60:1, default grey badge 3.84:1. Collapsed-strip role badges drop to 9.5 pt. These badges are the non-color backup for tally, so their legibility matters more than usual.
findings.evidence: Computed: badge.red #ff6961 on rgba(255,69,58,.2)=3.97; role.air white on #ff453a@92% over video=3.60; badge default=3.84. main-collapsed.html collapsed badges 'height:16px;font-size:9.5px'.
findings.scenario: Glancing at a collapsed strip mid-meeting, the operator can't read the tiny 'On air' badge, and the red tint alone doesn't disambiguate from REC.
findings.recommendation: Badges minimum 10.5 pt semibold. Use a darker red fill (systemRed at 100% with white bold text measures ≈4:1 — use bold 13 pt or a dark text on lighter red) or keep the tinted style but with primary text color. Verify with Increase Contrast.
alternatives: Use text-only role labels in primary color with a colored leading dot
Make the ON AIR pill a solid tally light and put the words beside it

findings.location: tally rings on pictures (red on air, green next, orange paused/skipped)
findings.issue: The rings have low contrast against typical video: red 1.62:1, green 2.72:1, orange 2.68:1 vs a mid-tone scene, all below the 3:1 non-text minimum. Red vs orange luminance differs only 1.66:1, so paused (orange) and on air (red) rings look alike. Text badges rescue the pictures, but the ring is presented as the primary signal in the legend.
findings.evidence: r3.css .onair::after inset 4px red, .next::after 3px green; computed vs #7a6553. states.html uses an orange ring for 'Skipped by Auto' and paused (standalone).
findings.scenario: A protan user sees Feed 1 (on air, red ring) and Feed 2 (paused, orange ring) as the same dark outline; only the small badges differ.
findings.recommendation: Add a contrasting inner and outer hairline (white 1 pt inside, black 1 pt outside) to every ring so it reads on any video. Distinguish states by pattern as well as hue (solid = on air, dashed = cutting/queued, double = paused). Keep the badge mandatory. Spec §7 already plans ring 4 → 5 pt under Increase Contrast; add the hairline by default.
alternatives: Move tally into a solid tally bar above the picture (broadcast-style) instead of a ring over video
Reserve rings for Program only; show paused/skipped only in the badge

findings.location: hover-only controls: picture hover group (Freeze, Clean, Zoom, Detach), collapsed strip hover (Pause, Stop), Four Up hover toolbar
findings.issue: Several controls appear only on pointer hover, with no keyboard focus reveal or VoiceOver path defined. Spec §7 defines a Tab order but doesn't say hover-revealed controls appear when focus enters the picture or strip, and there's no keyboard way to reveal the collapsed strip's Pause/Stop besides expanding.
findings.evidence: four-up legend 5: 'At rest only the name, state, timecode and REC stay visible'; main-collapsed legend 2: 'Hovering a collapsed strip reveals its inline controls'; spec §7 keyboard bullet has no focus-reveal rule.
findings.scenario: A keyboard-only or Switch Control user can't freeze a picture or pause one feed's recording in Four Up without the mouse.
findings.recommendation: Rule: anything revealed on hover is also revealed when keyboard focus or VoiceOver focus enters the container, and stays exposed to accessibility at all times (accessibilityElement children always present, hidden only visually). Every hover action also has a menu command and a context-menu item (already true for Freeze/Clean; add Pause/Stop Recording for the focused feed).
alternatives: Show hover controls permanently at reduced opacity when 'Full Keyboard Access' is on
Put Pause/Stop for the focused feed in the Record menu with ⌘R / ⌥⌘P

findings.location: live-control hit targets: strip chevron (18 pt), Processing switch (28×16 pt), collapsed record button (30 pt), cut-key badges, ⋯ (24 pt)
findings.issue: Some live controls are under the 24 pt minimum from the audit plan. The expand chevron is 18×18. The strip Processing switch is a mini switch 16 pt tall, and toggling it mid-meeting bypasses the whole pipeline. The off switch track contrast vs window is 1.65:1 (mockup rendering).
findings.evidence: r3.css .strip3 .chev 18px; kit.css .switch.sm 28×16; r3.js strip(): '<div class="switch sm on">' beside fx chips; computed fill3 track vs window 1.65.
findings.scenario: Using a trackpad during a call, the user misses the 18 pt chevron and hits the adjacent Processing switch, bypassing effects in Zoom.
findings.recommendation: Minimum 24×24 hit area for chevron and ⋯ (padding, not glyph size). Use a regular or small native switch with a text label ('Processing') rather than an unlabeled mini switch beside chips. Keep ≥ 8 pt spacing between disruptive and benign controls.
alternatives: Move Processing into the ⋯ popover and the toolbar/menu (⇧⌘B), leaving the strip with read-only chips
Make the whole collapsed strip header the disclosure target (click name area to expand)

findings.location: text below 10 pt: collapsed effect chips 9.5 pt, collapsed role badges 9.5 pt, shot timer and timeline labels 9.5 pt, k2 section labels 10 pt
findings.issue: Informational text is set at 9.5 pt in collapsed strips and timeline marks, below the macOS minimum readable size (Apple uses 10 pt caption2 as the floor). It doesn't scale with the system text-size setting.
findings.evidence: r3.js fxChips small 'font-size:9.5px'; main-collapsed.html/program-view.html .marks 9.5px; r2.css .shot .mkl 9.5px; .k2 10px.
findings.scenario: On a 13-inch display at default scaling the collapsed chips and cut-reason labels are unreadable without leaning in.
findings.recommendation: Floor at 10 pt (caption2) for any information; use semantic text styles (.caption2) so the macOS text size setting and accessibility zoom apply. If collapsed rows can't fit, drop chips rather than shrinking them.
alternatives: Replace collapsed chips with a single 'Effects 3/4' label
Show chips only on hover/expand

findings.issue: The VoiceOver plan labels elements but defines no announcements for live events that a non-visual or eyes-elsewhere user must hear: cut happened or queued, recording started/stopped/failed, signal lost, disk low, Auto skipped a source. Continuously changing values (elapsed time, timecode, meters at 2 Hz) risk chatty output if exposed as live regions.
findings.evidence: spec.html §7: labels for pictures, meters 'updates throttled to 2 Hz for speech'; no mention of AccessibilityNotification.Announcement or which events announce.
findings.scenario: A blind or low-vision presenter relying on VoiceOver isn't told that Feed 1's recording stopped after a source error until they explore the strip.
findings.recommendation: Add an announcement table to spec §7: announce state transitions only (Recording started/stopped/failed, Cut to Feed 2, Signal lost on Feed 3, 12 minutes left on 8TB), priority high for errors. Never auto-announce timers or meters; expose them as values read on focus.
alternatives: Optional 'Speak status changes' setting in General
Mirror announcements as system notifications when the app is in the background

findings.issue: Light appearance is shown only for one channel column, the dropdown top and the status bar (spec §8). Sidebar, ⋯ popover, Settings, menus, states, diagnostics and tool popovers are dark-only. The light sample's own secondary text measures 3.5:1 on #f5f5f7.
findings.evidence: spec.html §8 .light overrides; computed light label2 rgba(60,60,67,.62) on #f5f5f7 = 3.50, label3 = 1.85.
findings.scenario: A user in Light mode gets an untested sidebar where glass over a bright wallpaper washes out secondary text.
findings.recommendation: Round 4: render the main window (sidebar + strips + status bar), the ⋯ popover and one dropdown in Light. Check secondary text on glass over a bright wallpaper. Rely on system colors in code.
alternatives: Add a light/dark toggle to the mockup kit so every page can be viewed both ways

findings.location: picture click-to-cut and focus semantics for assistive tech
findings.issue: The picture has three meanings on click (cut, focus tile, select feed), and its VoiceOver element is described as one element with a label. The default VoiceOver action (VO-Space) on a picture is undefined: would it cut Program? An accidental activation by an AT user would cut a live meeting.
findings.evidence: spec §7: 'one element per picture'; main-expanded legend 2: 'Click a picture or press ⌃1/⌃2 to cut'; monitor-tools: focus by click.
findings.scenario: A VoiceOver user navigating pictures presses VO-Space to hear details and cuts Zoom to the wrong camera.
findings.recommendation: The picture's default accessibility action is 'Focus' (non-destructive). Cutting is a named custom action ('Cut to Feed 2') and a separate button, never the default. Aligns with fixing S1 for everyone.
alternatives: Expose 'Cut' only via the cut buttons and ⌃n; pictures have no activation action

findings.issue: The proposed red recording dot and orange attention dot on the menu bar icon are tiny color-only marks (red vs orange 1.66:1 luminance difference). They're indistinguishable for many color-blind users and invisible against some wallpapers on a transparent menu bar.
findings.evidence: menubar.html icon states card; settings General 'Show recording dot / attention dot'; main-expanded menubar markup: 6×6 px dot.
findings.scenario: A deuteranopic user can't tell whether the dot means 'recording' or 'problem'.
findings.recommendation: Differentiate by symbol, not hue: recording = video.fill with a small filled circle badge; attention = exclamationmark.triangle badge (or a distinct SF Symbol variant). Template image so it adapts to menu bar appearance. accessibilityLabel states the full status (already noted).
alternatives: Swap the whole icon to record.circle while recording and to exclamationmark.triangle on attention

findings.location: recording vs paused vs stopped states on the record button and REC pills
findings.issue: Paused vs recording is distinguished mostly by color (red vs orange) on the dots in sidebar rows and collapsed strips. The red/orange pair differs by 1.66:1, while the round record control's recording vs idle (square vs circle) is a good shape cue.
findings.evidence: standalone sidebar rows 'dot red' vs 'dot orange'; four-up collapsed Feed 4 'dot orange' + 'Paused 04:12' text; computed red vs orange 1.66.
findings.scenario: In Four Up, a color-blind user skims the dots to confirm every camera is rolling and misses the paused one.
findings.recommendation: Pair the paused dot with a pause glyph (⏸) instead of a plain orange dot; text is already present in most places — make the glyph the rule in compact contexts (sidebar, dropdown rows, status bar).
alternatives: Use SF Symbols record.circle.fill / pause.circle.fill everywhere instead of dots

findings.location: Reduce Transparency / Increase Contrast / Reduce Motion coverage
findings.issue: Spec §7 covers Reduce Transparency for glass and overlays, Increase Contrast for rings and separators, and Reduce Motion for meters and REC. It omits the shot timer progress, the director timeline 'now' line, cut transitions and popover/sheet animations. Increase Contrast doesn't address the low-contrast tertiary text or the badges.
findings.evidence: spec.html §7 lines on Reduce Transparency, Increase Contrast, Motion.
findings.scenario: With Reduce Motion on, the shot timer still animates continuously in the sidebar.
findings.recommendation: Extend §7: under Reduce Motion, shot timer and timeline update in 1 s steps without easing; under Increase Contrast, tertiary text → secondary, badges get 1 pt borders, effect chips get outlines, overlays get opaque capsules.

findings.issue: Sidebar secondary text on the floating glass measures 4.70:1, marginal for 10.5–11 pt captions. Tertiary measures 2.53:1. Contrast depends on the wallpaper behind the translucent sidebar, so a bright wallpaper will push secondary below 4.5:1.
findings.evidence: computed label2 on sidebar glass (rgba(48,48,52,.6) over a dim wallpaper) = 4.70; label3 = 2.53. Sidebar captions use 10.5 px (r3.css .sb3 .mini-row small).
findings.scenario: With a light wallpaper, sidebar rows such as '12:31 · 27.5 GB · ProRes 422' and '1 h 35 m left' fade.
findings.recommendation: Keep sidebar captions ≥ 11 pt secondary; rely on the system sidebar material (which adapts its tint) rather than custom translucency; verify against a white wallpaper.

findings.location: Nouns for the user-facing source object
findings.issue: The same object is called 'Feed' and 'Camera' interchangeably, even inside one menu.
findings.evidence: app-menus Feed menu: 'Add Camera' sits next to 'Rename Feed 1…' and 'Remove Feed 1'. Sidebar section header 'Cameras' (r3.js sidebar). Strip ⋯ popover footer 'Remove Camera' (main-collapsed). Settings: 'Per-Camera Folders' and 'Remove Camera' (the extension). Default names are 'Feed 1', the virtual camera is 'Ultracam · Feed 1', and the menu is 'Feed'.
findings.scenario: The user looks for 'Remove Camera' in the Feed menu and finds 'Remove Feed'. 'Remove Camera' in Settings removes the system extension, not a feed, so the shared word risks a destructive mix-up.
findings.recommendation: Use 'Feed' for the app object (menu name, default names, sidebar section 'Feeds', Add Feed…, Rename Feed…, Remove Feed). Reserve 'camera' for the physical device and the virtual camera ('Ultracam camera', Install/Remove Ultracam Camera).
alternatives: Rename the object 'Camera' everywhere and default names to 'Camera 1'; the virtual camera becomes 'Ultracam · Camera 1'
findings.decision_for_user: Feed or Camera as the user-facing noun

findings.issue: Stop has seven names, and one command is named differently in different places.
findings.evidence: Bare 'Stop' (strip, meaning stop recording); 'Stop Feed'; 'Stop Feeds' (menubar a, spec); 'Stop All Feeds' (menubar c, standalone) for the same command; 'Stop Recording'; 'Stop All Recordings'; 'Stop All' (app-menus table, diagnostics popover, standalone toolbar). The toolbar record button shows a stop glyph with only '12:31 · 2'.
findings.scenario: After a meeting the user wants to stop the backup takes but keep the feed for Zoom. Bare 'Stop' and unlabelled toolbar buttons make it unclear which one ends what.
findings.recommendation: Always use verb + object: Stop Recording / Stop All Recordings / Stop Feed / Stop All Feeds. Never a bare 'Stop'; an icon-only button gets the full name as its tooltip and accessibility label.
alternatives: Use 'End Take' for recordings to separate the verbs entirely

findings.issue: The same toolbar control is labelled four ways, and only one page shows the companion Pause All.
findings.evidence: '12:31 · 2' (main-expanded, main-collapsed, program-view), '12:31 · 3' (four-up), '12:31' (single), 'Stop All · 12:31' with a separate 'Pause All' button (standalone only).
findings.scenario: The user can't tell whether the red '12:31 · 2' button stops everything, opens a menu, or shows a count.
findings.recommendation: One rule: idle 'Record All'; recording 'Stop All · 12:31', with a count badge when there's more than one take. Pause All either always sits beside it or lives only in the menu.
alternatives: Make it a split button: main action Stop All, with a menu for Pause All and per-feed stop

findings.issue: ⌘0 is assigned to two different commands.
findings.evidence: monitor-tools keyboard card: 'Zoom in / out, ⌘0 to fit', and its zoom menu shows 'Fit ⌘0'. app-menus Window menu and spec §6 assign ⌘0 to the main window. monitor-tools' ⌘= / ⌘− zoom keys appear in neither app-menus' View ▸ Zoom nor the spec table.
findings.scenario: The user presses ⌘0 expecting the zoomed picture to return to Fit; the main window comes forward instead.
findings.recommendation: Keep ⌘0 for the main window (common macOS convention). Picture zoom uses ⌘= / ⌘− / ⌘9 for Fit, or menu-only. List them in app-menus View ▸ Zoom and in the spec table.
alternatives: Drop zoom shortcuts and use the zoom pop-up only

findings.issue: ⌘1–⌘4 means 'Select Feed' in the menus but 'Focus feed (keyboard target)' in the spec. Selection and focus are different concepts.
findings.evidence: app-menus Feed menu has a 'Select Feed' section with ⌘1/⌘2; its legend says the Feed menu acts on the selected feed and ⌘1–⌘4 change it. spec §6: '⌘1–⌘4 Focus feed (keyboard target)'; spec §7: '⌘1–⌘4 move focus between feeds'.
findings.scenario: The engineer implements ⌘2 as keyboard focus only; ⇧⌘B then still bypasses Feed 1 while the user believes Feed 2 is targeted.
findings.recommendation: Define one concept, either a single 'selected feed' or 'focused picture', that drives the Feed menu, ⇧⌘B and the picture shortcuts. Show it visibly, and use the same wording in the menus, spec and legends.
alternatives: Remove the selected-feed concept; Feed-menu items become per-feed submenus

findings.issue: The two automation settings each have three or four different wordings, not just case variants.
findings.evidence: Start: 'Start with camera apps' (sidebar), 'Start with Camera Apps' (dropdown), 'Start When Camera Is in Use' (app-menus), 'Start when camera is in use' (Settings; also the current app's label). Record: 'Record with camera apps' / 'Record with Camera Apps' / 'Record when a camera app opens Ultracam' (Settings).
findings.scenario: The user turns on 'Record when a camera app opens Ultracam' in Settings and doesn't recognise it as the 'Record with camera apps' switch in the sidebar.
findings.recommendation: One wording pair, with case following context (menus title case, forms sentence case): 'Start with Camera Apps' / 'Record with Camera Apps'. Settings can add the explanation as a footnote.
alternatives: Keep the current app's 'Start when camera is in use' and use 'Record when camera is in use'

findings.issue: A paused feed has an orange ring on one page and no ring on another, and the spec's tally table has no paused row.
findings.evidence: standalone: Feed 2 paused has an orange ring plus an orange 'PAUSED 04:12' pill (its legend says so). four-up: Feed 4 paused has the pill only. spec §5 picture-tally roles: On air / Next / Consumer on air / Idle, with no Paused. The tile() builder has no paused state; standalone patches it with string replace.
findings.scenario: Two pages built from the same spec show paused differently, so engineering has to guess.
findings.recommendation: Rings are reserved for tally (Program or a consumer). Paused is shown by the orange pill and the strip state only. Add a paused state to tile() and strip(), and a row to the spec table.
alternatives: Use an orange ring for paused everywhere and add it to the spec

findings.issue: Strips and status bars were hand-built or string-patched on five pages, and those copies have drifted from the builders.
findings.evidence: main-collapsed builds both collapsed strips by hand; its hover row drops the effect chips. states uses its own sbox() helper, whose collapsed recording row still shows '0 drops', which the builder removed. four-up hand-builds the Feed 3/4 strips and its status bar. standalone patches builder output for paused and writes its own status bar. spec's status bar omits '(video)' after GPU and the Audio segment. Grep counts: hand-built strip3 = main-collapsed 2, four-up 2, states 2; hand-built sbar = four-up, standalone, spec, states.
findings.scenario: Round-4 builder fixes won't reach the pages that bypass the builders, so inconsistencies multiply.
findings.recommendation: Extend the builders and rebuild those pages with them. strip(): states ready / no-folder / recording / paused / finishing / failed / stopped / waiting / unsupported / bypass, and a hover variant. tile(): paused / no-signal / unsupported / hidden. statusbar(): a segment list parameter.

findings.issue: The processed signal is called 'Output' on pictures but 'Processed Output' in the scope popover and in Settings.
findings.evidence: Picture pills (tile builder): 'Output'. monitor-tools Scopes popover: Signal 'Source | Output' in one place and 'Processed Output' in others. Settings Monitor pane: Picture signal 'Source | Processed Output'. The current code (MonitorTileChrome) uses 'Processed Output'.
findings.scenario: The user picks 'Output' on the picture and then can't find the same option by name in Settings.
findings.recommendation: Use 'Output' everywhere in the UI, with the help text 'Processed output, as published'. Keep 'Processed Output' only in diagnostics if needed.
alternatives: Use 'Processed Output' everywhere, matching the current code

findings.issue: Opening a picture in its own window has five names.
findings.evidence: Detach (hover button), Detach to Window (tile context menu), Detach Focused Picture (View ▸ Layout submenu), Window ▸ Detach Monitor ›, and Open Monitor Window (Feed menu, dropdown submenu).
