findings.scenario: The user learns 'Detach' on the picture but can't find it in the menus.
findings.recommendation: Command 'Open in Monitor Window', with Window ▸ Monitor Windows › listing open ones. The hover button is the same icon with that tooltip.
alternatives: 'Detach' everywhere

findings.issue: One setting has two different controls and names.
findings.evidence: app-menus Ultracam menu: toggle 'Hide from Dock (menu bar only)'. Settings General: 'Show Ultracam in: Dock and menu bar | Menu bar only' (its caption references today's 'Hide from Dock').
findings.scenario: The user unchecks 'Hide from Dock' and Settings now reads 'Dock and menu bar', which is two mental models for one setting.
findings.recommendation: Use the same wording in both: either the 'Show in Dock' toggle everywhere, or the segmented 'Dock and menu bar / Menu bar only' in Settings with the menu item mirroring it as 'Show in Dock'.

findings.location: Effect names and the master switch
findings.issue: Effects are named by value in some places and by function in others, and the master switch is called both 'Processing' and 'Effects'.
findings.evidence: Strip chips: 'LUT · 1080p · 4:2:0 · 29.97'. ⋯ popover: '1 · LUT / 2 · Downscale / 3 · Color / 4 · Frame rate'. Menus: '2 · Downscale to 1080p', '3 · Color 4:2:0 8-bit', '4 · Limit to 29.97 fps'. Signal path: '3 · 4:2:0 8-bit'. Master switch: 'Processing' in the menus and popover; 'Effects active' result line; the strip switch has no label.
findings.scenario: The user can't map the '4:2:0' chip to 'Color' in the popover, or tell what the unlabelled strip switch does.
findings.recommendation: Master switch is always 'Processing' (off = bypass). The items are 'effects', each with a fixed name plus value: 'LUT', 'Downscale · 1080p', 'Color · 4:2:0 8-bit', 'Frame rate · 29.97'. Chips can show the value with the name as tooltip and accessibility label. Label the strip switch 'Processing'.
alternatives: Chips show names (LUT, Scale, Color, Rate) and the value appears on hover

findings.issue: 'Next' and 'queued' are used for the same Program state, and a third word covers a different state.
findings.evidence: Picture 'NEXT', strip 'Next', program-view cut bar 'Feed 2 queued', spec 'Queued'. states adds 'CUTTING…' / 'Cut pending' for a manual cut awaiting the frame boundary.
findings.scenario: The user sees NEXT on the picture and 'queued' in the cut bar and wonders whether these are two different things.
findings.recommendation: 'Next' means the director's planned cut (green). 'Cutting…' means a manual cut waiting for the frame boundary (dashed red). Drop 'queued'.

findings.issue: One icon is used for unrelated commands.
findings.evidence: The 'sliders' icon is used for Effects (menubar, single dropdown, app-menus), Rename Feed 1… (app-menus), Collapse All Strips (app-menus View) and the toolbar collapse toggle (r3.js toolbar). The sparkle 'auto' icon is used for both Automatic Switching and Start with Camera Apps.
findings.scenario: The toolbar collapse button looks like an effects control.
findings.recommendation: Assign distinct SF Symbols in the spec: effects 'slider.horizontal.3'; collapse strips 'rectangle.compress.vertical' / 'chevron.up.chevron.down'; rename 'pencil'; auto switching 'wand.and.stars'; start with camera apps 'video.badge.checkmark' or none.

findings.issue: Elapsed time and time remaining use mixed formats.
findings.evidence: Elapsed: '00:12:31' (expanded strip), '12:31' (collapsed strip, sidebar, toolbar, REC pill), '1:42:10' (states). Remaining: '1 h 35 m left', '1 h 05 m left', '12 min left', '3 h 10 m available' (states status bar).
findings.scenario: Minor, but numbers that shift format draw the eye and look like different quantities.
findings.recommendation: Elapsed is m:ss under 1 h and h:mm:ss after, everywhere (tabular digits). Remaining is '1 h 35 min left' / '12 min left'; never 'available'.
alternatives: Always h:mm:ss for elapsed

findings.issue: Identical scenarios show different time left, because the rule (does a paused take count?) is undefined.
findings.evidence: standalone: Feed 1 recording to 8TB and Feed 2 paused, writing to Archive. Sidebar, strip and status bar show 8TB '3 h 10 m left', which is correct for one writer. The states status-bar card for the same scenario shows '8TB 1 h 35 m'. main-expanded and program-view: Feed 1 → 8TB and Feed 2 → Archive (strip 'Own folder'), yet 8TB shows '1 h 35 m', as if both write to it. four-up: '8TB 1 h 05 m' with no stated per-drive split.
findings.scenario: The engineer can't derive the formula from the mockups; the user sees the number jump when pausing.
findings.recommendation: Define time left per drive = free space ÷ combined data rate of the active takes writing to that drive (a paused take holds 0 rate). Then fix main-expanded and states to match: 8TB has only Feed 1, so 3 h 10 m.

findings.issue: The status bar has no fixed segment order; segments appear or disappear per page.
findings.evidence: Builder: output → Program → REC → Audio → resources. standalone: adds 'Timecode: PC time' and drops Audio. four-up: drops Audio and adds a warning. spec: drops Audio, and writes 'GPU' instead of 'GPU (video)'. states: the error variant leads with 'Couldn't start Feed 1 · Retry'.
findings.scenario: Segments jump around between sessions, so the user can't learn where to look.
findings.recommendation: Fixed order: [problem, only when present, leftmost] · output → consumer · Program (Program mode only) · recording · audio · spacer · resources. Timecode mode belongs in the recording popover.

findings.location: Feed state wording in Separate mode
findings.issue: In Separate mode the picture and the strip describe the same state differently.
findings.evidence: single: picture badge 'ON AIR · Zoom', strip output row 'Ultracam · Feed 1 · In use by Zoom', sidebar 'In use by Zoom'. Program mode is consistent ('ON AIR · Program' and 'On air in Program').
findings.scenario: Minor: two phrasings for one state.
findings.recommendation: The badge stays 'ON AIR · Zoom'; the strip and sidebar read 'On air in Zoom' (or both say 'In use by Zoom'). Pick one.

findings.issue: The window title follows no rule.
findings.evidence: 'Meeting', 'Meeting · Program view', 'Recording Session' (four-up), 'Recording' (standalone), 'Feed 1' (single).
findings.scenario: Polish only.
findings.recommendation: Title 'Ultracam'. The subtitle is derived: '<n> feeds · Program → Zoom · recording 2' or '<n> feeds · recording · not in a meeting'.
alternatives: The title states the session type, derived from consumer and recording state

findings.issue: The same proposed shortcut is tagged NEW on some pages and not others.
findings.evidence: ⌥⌘R is tagged NEW in the single and standalone dropdowns, untagged in menubar (a, b, c, g) and the states dropdowns, and marked 'PROPOSED' in the app-menus table. ⌃⌥A and ⌃1 are untagged in most dropdowns.
findings.scenario: Reviewers can't trust the NEW tag as a complete list of proposals.
findings.recommendation: Either tag every proposed shortcut on every page, or tag none on pages and keep the single list in the app-menus/spec shortcut tables (preferred: less noise).

findings.location: Start/Stop Feed control in the window
findings.issue: The running strip and toolbar have no Stop Feed control, but the stopped strip has Start Feed, so the control appears only in one direction.
findings.evidence: r3 toolbar() has no Start/Stop. The builder's expanded strip header has no Stop Feed (r2 V2 had 'Stop Feed'). states' 'Feed stopped' strip shows a 'Start Feed' button. While running, stopping is reachable only through ⌘↩ / the menus / the dropdown.
findings.scenario: The user wants to release the capture device for another app and can't find Stop Feed in the window.
findings.recommendation: Put a Start/Stop Feed control in the same place in both states (the strip header, or the ⋯ popover footer), labelled per L7-02.
alternatives: Toolbar Start/Stop for the selected feed

findings.location: Program mode with Feed 1 (2160p59.94, frame-rate limit off) and Feed 2 (2160p29.97)
findings.issue: Cutting between Program sources whose processed output differs in size, chroma or frame rate disconnects and reconnects the Program camera sink on every cut. The mocked configuration does exactly this, and the UI neither prevents nor warns.
findings.evidence: ProgramOutputBridge.sameContract compares width/height/pixelFormat/duration; reconnectLocked(to:) rebuilds the sink when a cut frame is rejected with 'negotiated format'. AppModel.reconcileProgramTransportDemand derives the contract from the on-air producer's configuration. r3.js FEEDS: f1 2160p 59.94 with fx [1,1,1,0] (limit off) gives 59.94 output; f2 2160p 29.97 gives 29.97 output.
findings.scenario: Each cut between Feed 1 and Feed 2 drops or blinks Zoom's picture while the sink renegotiates.
findings.recommendation: Add a Program output format, or enforce a shared contract across Program sources. Flag any source whose output differs, in its strip and in the sidebar's Program section. Block or warn before entering Program with mismatched sources.
alternatives: Auto-enable the frame-rate limit on 59.94 sources in Program mode
Show a 'format differs from Program' badge on the source picture

findings.location: Signal path / dropdown stat / Delivered rows
findings.issue: Mock data contradicts the pipeline: Feed 1 is 2160p59.94 with effect 4 (frame-rate limit) off, yet the pages show '1080p29.97' to Zoom and 'Delivered 29.97 fps'.
findings.evidence: single.html:120,127 (step 4 struck through, then 'Zoom 1080p29.97'); single.html:61 and menubar.html:127 '1080p29.97'; diagnostics.html:88 'Delivered 29.97 fps'; r3.js FEEDS.f1 fx [1,1,1,0].
findings.scenario: A reviewer or engineer learns the wrong rule: that 59.94 sources reach Zoom at 29.97 without the limit.
findings.recommendation: Make the values consistent: either show 1080p59.94, or turn on effect 4 for Feed 1 in FEEDS and in every hand-written copy.

findings.location: Channel strip effect chips, processing switch, LUT, and ⋯ popover settings for non-selected feeds
findings.issue: Independent per-feed output controls are shown as if they already exist, but AppModel edits only the selected feed. configuration, pipelineEnabled, gamut, LUT state, previewEnabled and automaticFeedEnabled are selected-feed singletons loaded by applySelectedDescriptor, and chooseLUT acts on selectedFeedID.
findings.evidence: AppModel.swift applySelectedDescriptor (~544-571), selectFeed (422-439), chooseLUT (342). Headless feeds use descriptor.configuration only at start (startFeed 659-680).
findings.scenario: The user flips Feed 2's LUT chip in its strip. Nothing in the model can apply it today without first selecting Feed 2, which reloads its LUT and rebinds both previews.
findings.recommendation: Treat per-feed controls as a NEW model refactor: per-feed view models that own configuration, pipeline, LUT, gamut, automatic and preview state, routed through feedCoordinator.reconfigureCapture(feedID:). List it first in the implementation plan.
alternatives: Keep the selected-feed model, and make interacting with a strip visibly select that feed

findings.location: Per-feed audio meters, Live · format badges, timecode, delivered/drops, Diagnostics Feed 2 tab, status-bar Audio popover
findings.issue: Live stats for non-selected feeds have no data source: capture updates from any feed other than the selected one are discarded.
findings.evidence: AppModel.installCaptureUpdateHandler has 'guard self.selectedFeedID == feedID else { return }' before 'self.update = update'. Only recording statistics are tracked per feed (RecordingModel.feeds[].statistics).
findings.scenario: Feed 2's strip meters and the Diagnostics Feed 2 tab would stay empty or show stale values.
findings.recommendation: NEW: keep a CaptureUpdate per FeedID and drive strips, diagnostics and status popovers from it.

findings.location: Toolbar Stop, dropdown 'Stop Feeds' / 'Stop All Feeds', strip 'Stop Feed'
findings.issue: Stop is misrepresented. AppModel.stop() stops only the selected feed, in both modes. In Program mode the headless sources keep running, and the Program transport can stay up if the on-air producer is headless. stop() also ends the selected feed's recording without saying so.
findings.evidence: AppModel.stop() 701-710 calls feedCoordinator.stop(selectedFeedID) and recordingModel.stop(feedID: selectedFeedID). FeedCoordinator.stop(_:) stops one session. reconcileProgramTransportDemand only requires the on-air producer to be running.
findings.scenario: After a Program meeting the user presses Stop. Feed 2 (headless, possibly on air) keeps capturing and Zoom keeps receiving Program.
findings.recommendation: Define explicit commands and runtime APIs: Stop Feed N (warns that it ends Feed N's recording) and Stop All Feeds / End Session (stops every source and the Program route). Label the toolbar Stop with what it stops.
findings.verified: AppModel.swift:701-709 stop() uses selectedFeedID and stops its recording

findings.location: Per-strip Start Feed / Stop Feed for a non-selected feed
findings.issue: No model API starts or stops an arbitrary feed. start() and stop() use selectedFeedID, and other feeds start only through the automatic policy or as Program headless sources.
findings.evidence: AppModel.start()/startFeed()/stop(); reconcileAutomaticFeed starts non-selected feeds with startCapture(feedID:).
findings.scenario: Pressing 'Start Feed' on Feed 2's strip in Separate mode has nothing to call without changing the selection.
findings.recommendation: NEW runtime API start(feedID:)/stop(feedID:) that handles preview ownership and camera output enable per feed.

findings.location: Green NEXT ring / 'queued' / 'Cut to Feed 2 at the next speech gap after 10 s' / 'Auto holds Feed 1 for 1.8 s more'
findings.issue: A persistent NEXT and a hold countdown imply the director exposes its planned next camera and remaining hold time. It doesn't. The model only exposes switcherPendingFeedID: a decision queued until the next Program frame boundary, normally about one frame.
findings.evidence: AppModel.switcherPendingFeedID = feedCoordinator.programOutput.pendingFeedID. AutoSwitcherBridge returns instructions and has no forecast API. menubar.html:100 'Auto holds Feed 1 for 1.8 s more'.
findings.scenario: Users trust a NEXT indicator the runtime can't produce, or engineers end up fabricating it.
findings.recommendation: This is an unmarked invention. Either tag it NEW and add a bridge API for candidate and hold state, or redesign: green means a pending cut (brief), plus a shot timer built from the applied-decision time and the configured min/soft/max (feasible today).
alternatives: Show 'eligible to cut after the minimum shot' instead of a predicted target

findings.location: Director timeline speech lanes per camera
findings.issue: The director hears one audio stream (the selected feed's embedded audio, max of L/R), not speech per camera, so per-camera speech lanes would be fabricated.
findings.evidence: AppModel.feedAutoSwitcherAudio ingests update.audioRMS/Peak from the selected feed only. AutoSwitcherTimelineRecorder records a single AudioCue stream plus decisions with reason and forced flags.
findings.scenario: A timeline showing Feed 2 'speaking' misleads users about why the director cut.
findings.recommendation: Keep the timeline (NEW) but show one speech lane (naming its source feed), plus the on-air lanes and the cut reasons and forced flags the recorder already has.

findings.issue: Transcript assisted is the default mode, but the app has no built-in speech recognizer. Transcript cues only arrive if an external adapter calls ingestAutoSwitcherTranscript, and the UI presents the mode without a caveat.
findings.evidence: AppSettingsStore NaturalTalkingHeadSettings mode = .transcriptAssisted; the comment above AppModel.ingestAutoSwitcherTranscript says 'The app currently has no built-in speech recognizer'. settings.html:160.
findings.scenario: The user picks Transcript assisted expecting word-aware cuts, but it behaves as audio-only.
findings.recommendation: Add the caption 'No transcript source connected — cuts use audio only' together with the connection state, or default to Low latency until an ASR source exists.
findings.verified: no Speech framework import in Sources

findings.location: Right column shows Luma Waveform and RGB Parade at the same time for Feed 1
findings.issue: A feed can show only one scope mode today; MonitorScopeSettings has a single 'mode'.
findings.evidence: MonitorConfiguration.swift MonitorScopeSettings { enabled, mode, gain, graticule, refreshHz }.
findings.scenario: Engineers can't build the page as drawn without a config/schema change and twice the scope cost.
findings.recommendation: Show one scope per feed with a mode toggle, or mark multiple scopes as NEW with a MonitorScopeSettings change.

findings.location: Rename…, Add Camera, Output mode 'Change while stopped'
findings.issue: Topology edits are locked while any source is active OR any recording is active. The ⋯ popover and the Feed menu show Rename enabled during a live, recording session, and the lock message leaves out recording.
findings.evidence: AppModel.renameFeed/addFeed/removeFeed/setOutputMode all guard on canEditFeedTopology; FeedLifecycleDemandPolicy.canEditTopology = !loading && !sourceActive && !recordingActive. main-collapsed.html:129, app-menus.html:108.
findings.scenario: The user tries to rename Feed 1 mid-meeting and nothing happens.
findings.recommendation: Disable with the reason 'Stop all feeds and recordings to change'. NEW alternative: allow renaming while running, since it only changes names and the registry display.

findings.location: Sidebar Automation 'Start with camera apps' and the dropdown row
findings.issue: Shown as one session-wide switch, but automatic start is per feed (descriptor.automaticFeed). The current toggle is the selected feed's flag.
findings.evidence: AppModel.applySelectedDescriptor sets automaticFeedEnabled = descriptor.automaticFeed; reconcileAutomaticFeed iterates descriptors and reads descriptor.automaticFeed. r3.js sidebar() Automation rows.
findings.scenario: With two feeds, the switch silently controls only the selected one.
findings.recommendation: Either show it per feed (strip ⋯ / collapsed state) or make it a NEW global setting applied to all feeds, and say which feeds it covers.

findings.location: NEW 'Record with camera apps' + 'Stop when the last camera app closes'
findings.issue: Automatic mode treats an active or paused recording as demand and never stops a feed that is recording. Auto-recording would therefore keep capture alive after Zoom closes, unless the two rules are implemented together.
findings.evidence: AppModel.reconcileAutomaticFeed: policy.demand(camera || programRequested || recording); case .stop: guard ... !recording.
findings.scenario: Zoom closes, and the backup keeps recording and capture keeps running indefinitely.
findings.recommendation: Specify this as one coupled NEW feature (start a take on route demand; when demand ends, stop and finalize, then release capture) and show both rules as one control.

findings.issue: Mock throughput is unrealistic for ProRes 422 UHD: '18.4 GB · 184 Mb/s' after 12:31 at 2160p59.94. Apple's ProRes white paper gives about 943 Mb/s at 59.94 and about 471 Mb/s at 29.97. The time-left figures also don't follow from the free space shown.
findings.evidence: r3.js FEEDS f1 rec size/rate; settings '2.1 TB free · ~3 h 10 m'. RecordingStatistics already measures videoMegabitsPerSecond.
findings.scenario: The NEW time-left feature is designed around numbers 4–5× too low; real takes fill drives far faster.
findings.recommendation: Use realistic data, and base time left on the measured videoMegabitsPerSecond (using a codec/rate table until the first second is measured).

findings.location: Program picture in the dropdown and in Program view
findings.issue: previewRenderer and miniPreviewRenderer are bound to the selected feed, so a Program picture has to be a monitor surface (target 'program'). That's feasible, but it's an owned, size-limited picture under the monitor governor, not native passthrough.
findings.evidence: AppModel.selectFeed binds previewRenderer and miniPreviewRenderer to the selected feed; MonitorCoordinator.updateTargets(programAvailable:) provides the Program target.
findings.scenario: Under load the Program picture can degrade or be refused while the native feed picture doesn't, which looks like a bug.
findings.recommendation: Document this in spec §9, and design the 'monitor unavailable / reduced' state for Program pictures (dropdown and Program view).

findings.issue: Pages need more simultaneous pictures than there are native renderers. Every non-selected or Program picture is a monitor surface sharing one presentation/analysis budget, and that budget can refuse presentation ('insufficient presentation capacity'). The refusal state isn't designed.
findings.evidence: Counts: main-expanded 2 pictures + 2 scopes; main-collapsed 2 + 2 scopes; program-view 3; single 1 (+2 scopes, see L8-10); standalone 2 + 2 scopes, plus 2 in the dropdown; four-up 4 (1 native + 3 surfaces); menubar (a) 3 surfaces while open, (c) 2. README: 'Additional windows can report insufficient presentation capacity'.
findings.scenario: In Four Up, with the dropdown and a detached monitor open, a tile goes blank with no explanation.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Monitor unavailable — capacity' tile state with Retry, give the on-air picture priority, and note the budget in spec §9.

findings.location: Tool toggles without a master 'Monitor tools' switch
findings.issue: The current MonitorConfiguration keeps a toolsEnabled master switch, and the selected feed uses native passthrough only while tools are off. One-tap tools is a schema and behavior change, and turning any tool on switches that picture from native video to an owned monitor picture.
findings.evidence: MonitorToolsToolbar Toggle('Monitor tools', isOn: $configuration.toolsEnabled); MonitorBoundTile.usesNativePreview requires !toolsEnabled.
findings.scenario: Users don't know that tapping a tool changes that feed's picture path (latency and scaling).
findings.recommendation: Tag it NEW, derive toolsEnabled from 'any tool on' with a migration, and note the picture-path change in the spec.

findings.location: Unmarked inventions and a shortcut collision
findings.issue: Several items aren't in the app and aren't tagged NEW: ⌘= / ⌘− / ⌘0 zoom (monitor-tools keyboard card), 'Show Live Preview' (menubar d), 'Input settings…' (states No-signal tile), per-take progress in the quit sheet (today the app waits via terminateLater with no UI), and the orange 'Skipped by Auto' tally (source health exists but has no UI). app-menus also assigns ⌘0 to 'Main window', which collides with ⌘0 'fit'. 'Swap Pictures' already exists (Swap tiles), so it isn't an invention.
findings.evidence: monitor-tools keyboard card; menubar (d); states #4/#18; UltracamApp AppDelegate.applicationShouldTerminate → .terminateLater; MonitorWorkspaceShell 'Swap tiles'.
findings.scenario: Scope creep and contradictory shortcuts reach implementation.
findings.recommendation: Tag each one NEW and resolve ⌘0 (keep it for the main window; zoom to fit becomes ⌥⌘0, or View menu only).

findings.issue: The working tree changed during the session. False color is now Off / Sony S-Log3 / EL Zone (both gated on a Sony S-Log3 source), with an EL Zone exposure-offset stepper (−10…+10 in 0.25 steps) and 'Unsupported saved mode/input' for legacy ARRI settings.
